FAQ's

What is a business center?

A business center is a fully equipped workspace that provides various facilities and services to individuals or companies, including office spaces, meeting rooms, administrative support, and other amenities.

Are business centers suitable for short-term or long-term office needs?

Business centers are designed to accommodate both short-term and long-term office needs. They offer flexible lease terms, allowing businesses to rent office spaces for a few hours, days, months, or even years, depending on their requirements.

What services are typically offered in a business center?

Business centers commonly offer services such as furnished office spaces, virtual office solutions, coworking spaces, meeting and conference rooms, reception and administrative support, high-speed internet connectivity, telephone services, mail handling, and access to business equipment and facilities.

What is a virtual office, and how does it work?

A virtual office is a service offered by business centers that provides businesses with a professional business address, phone number, mail handling, and other administrative support, without the need for a physical office space. It allows businesses to establish a presence in a desirable location without the associated costs of a physical office.

Who can benefit from using a business center?

Business centers cater to a wide range of professionals and organizations, including startups, freelancers, small and medium-sized enterprises (SMEs), remote workers, satellite offices, and companies expanding into new markets or locations.

Can I hold meetings or events in a business center?

Yes, most business centers provide well-equipped meeting and conference rooms that can be rented on an hourly or daily basis. Some centers also offer event spaces for hosting seminars, workshops, or corporate events.

What are the advantages of using a business center?

Using a business center offers several advantages, including cost savings compared to traditional office setups, flexibility in terms of lease agreements and office space size, access to professional facilities and services, networking opportunities, a prestigious business address, and a supportive business environment.

Are there additional services available in business centers?

Many business centers offer additional services such as IT support, secretarial services, document printing and scanning, courier services, access to business lounges, on-site cafeterias or refreshment areas, fitness facilities, and parking facilities. The availability of these services may vary depending on the specific business center.

Can I customize my office space in a business center?

Depending on the business center, customization options may be available to meet specific requirements. Some centers offer flexible configurations and allow businesses to add their branding or personalize their workspace to a certain extent.

How do I choose the right business center for my needs?

When selecting a business center, consider factors such as location, accessibility, pricing and lease terms, available facilities and services, reputation, customer reviews, and the compatibility of the center’s offerings with your business requirements. It is recommended to visit the center in person or take virtual tours to assess the suitability before making a decision.

What is Tecom Freezone?
In Dubai, United Arab Emirates, there is a business hub called Tecom Freezone. It is one of Dubai’s biggest and most thriving free zones, providing entrepreneurs and enterprises with a variety of business-friendly rules, incentives, and infrastructure.
How long does it take to set up a business in Tecom Freezone?
Depending on the type of business and the level of application completion, the timeframe for establishing a business in Tecom Freezone may change. Nonetheless, it usually takes two to four weeks to complete the process.
What are the benefits of setting up a business in Tecom Freezone?
100% foreign ownership, tax exemption, faster company registration, access to cutting-edge infrastructure and facilities, and quick visa processing for staff are just a few advantages of establishing a firm in Tecom Freezone.
What are the costs associated with setting up a business in Tecom Freezone?
What types of businesses can be set up in Tecom Freezone?
Tecom Freezone caters to a wide range of business sectors, including media, information technology, education, healthcare, and more.
Do I need to have a physical office in Tecom Freezone to set up a business?
Absolutely, having a physical office or workspace inside the free zone is one of the conditions for establishing a firm in Tecom Freezone.
What is the process for setting up a business in Tecom Freezone?
A business must submit a business plan, choose a legal entity, apply for a trade license, and register with the Dubai Chamber of Business and Industry in order to establish a company in Tecom Freezone.
Can I operate my business outside of Tecom Freezone if I set it up there?
Yes, businesses set up in Tecom Freezone are allowed to operate outside of the free zone, as long as they comply with the regulations and requirements of the Dubai authorities.
What are the requirements for setting up a business in Tecom Freezone?
Depending on the type of business, different requirements may apply for establishing one in Tecom Freezone, although most frequently a valid passport, proof of address, financial records, and other pertinent documents are needed.
Is it mandatory to have a local sponsor to set up a business in Tecom Freezone?
No, one advantage of establishing a firm in Tecom Freezone is that there is no requirement for a local sponsor and 100% international ownership is permitted.

How long does it take to set up a company in Saudi Arabia?

What documents do you need to register a company in Saudi Arabia?

You will need passport copies of your shareholders and directors, your business plan, proof of address, and company incorporation documents if a foreign parent company is involved. For registering your company in KSA, you also need your Commercial Registration (CR), Memorandum of Association (MoA), and Articles of Association (AoA) attested by MoFA and the Saudi Embassy. Moreover, you might need additional approvals depending on your business activity.

What licenses are required to start a business in Saudi Arabia?

For starting your business in Saudi Arabia, you need an investment license from the Ministry of Investment, followed by commercial registration from the Ministry of Commerce.     A company’s official name is its trade name. The first step in registering a company is the trade name registration. All companies must reserve their trade name through trade name registration in Dubai before proceeding with issuance formalities.

    In this article, you will learn everything about trade name registration in Dubai. Let us observe:

    1. What is the difference between a trade name and a trademark?

    The terms trade name and trademark sound similar, but it is critical for business owners, especially those in the early stages of their venture, to understand the distinction. Choosing and registering trade names and trademarks is an important part of establishing a company’s and its products’ brand presence and recognition in the marketplace; so it is a process that you should take seriously.

    The law distinguishes between the two: a trade name refers to the company’s official name; whereas a trademark protects a company’s brand. While they are not the same, businesses should avoid selecting trade names that are too similar to a registered trademark, as this could expose owners to a potential lawsuit.

    1.2. Trade name

    A trade name is an official name under which a sole proprietor or company chooses to conduct business. They also refer to a trading name as a doing business as (DBA) name. Legally registering a trade name is an important step in a company’s branding, but it does not provide an unlimited brand name or legal protection for the use of the name.

    The requirements for registering a trading name vary by country, but most countries require registration with the state government or through a county clerk’s office. The practical function of registering a trade name is primarily for administrative and accounting purposes; such as filing a corporate tax return with the IRS in addition to your personal income tax return.

    Although registering a trading name does not provide legal protection in the same way that registering a trademark does, it is still important to choose a trading name carefully. This is because it is the first step in establishing your company’s identity in the marketplace. As previously stated, registering a trading name does not grant you trademark rights; this is a separate process.

    1.3. Trademark

    A trademark is a more important step in establishing brand recognition in the market. You can associate a trademark with or part of your business name; and you can use it to provide legal protection for the use of names, logos, symbols, or company slogans. Nike’s swoosh symbol and Coke’s “Coca-Cola” written in its distinctive script are two well-known trademarks.

    People easily identify trademarks because they include the trademark symbol—TM. You must register a trademark separately from a trading name, and this must be done at the federal level rather than the state level.

    The registration of a trademark grants an individual or business the exclusive use of the trademark, establishes legally that the trademark was not previously used by any other business entity prior to your registration of it; and provides official government protection from any other business infringing on your registered trademark.

    It also protects you from legal liability if someone later claims that you are infringing on a previously registered trademark. You or your company can register a trademark directly, or you can hire a lawyer who specializes in intellectual property law or trademark registration to do it for you. Here you can learn about trademark registration in the UAE.

    1.3.1. More details

    Having an intellectual property lawyer handle the registration adds an extra layer of assurance that the registration is done correctly and completely; and that a thorough investigation has been conducted to ensure that the trademark has not already been registered by another person or company.

    2. Why is it necessary to register a trade name in the UAE?

    Trade name registration in Sharjah, for example, is simply the registration of a company name in the UAE’s Economic Department. For registering your trade name, you must go to the Department of Economic Development.

    3. How long does it take to register a trade name?

    In Abu Dhabi, trade name registration takes no more than 24 hours, and you can reserve the company name within a day.

    4. Types of trade name registrations that have not been approved by the DED

    • Trade name registration in Dubai essentially means reserving a name for your company. A trade name can never be the same; other commercial entities must be different. Trade names must be distinct; if you register a similar name, authorities will not approve it.
    • A trade name is not registered in the UAE if it violates public order or morality. Additionally, DED Dubai does not approve of misleading trade names. The DED ensures that company names in the UAE are registered in accordance with commercial activity.
    • In addition, the business owner must ensure that the trade name registration does not include the name “Allah” (God) or any other religious name. Trade name registration in Dubai that is associated with the ruling authority is also prohibited.

    5. How do I register a trade name in the UAE?

    Trade name registration in the UAE is as simple as submitting an application to the Economic Department. However, you must submit documents with the application, and trade name reservation fees must be paid at the counter.

    In the UAE, you can register your trade name both online and offline. If you want us to register your trade name with the Economic Department, we can do so in the simplest way possible.

    6. How to verify a company’s registration in the UAE?

    Every registered firm in the country must have a trade license to operate. You can request a copy by email or look it up on the DED’s website. Trade licenses are not private documents because they must be displayed in any office or store. It is a public right to request or have this information referred to.

    Remember that the vast majority of shady businesses will provide you with an incorrect registration number. Furthermore, it is simple to verify and will keep you from entering into a difficult and unprofitable business arrangement.

    The enterprise has the right to leverage a trading name for another corporation that acquired the franchise right when presenting the franchise agreement to the Department of Economic Development.

    6.1. More details

    Trade name registration in Dubai is simple, and it is valid for six months. If the consumer’s trade name registration expires, he or she must re-register the name and pay all outstanding fees. If the trade name owner does not issue the trade license before the reserve period expires, the business name will be automatically canceled.

    The Department of Economic Development has the authority to cancel or amend a trade name if it is too similar to an existing trade name or does not correspond with the specified terms and conditions.

    7. What are the fees for registering a trade name?

    Trade name registration fees in the UAE vary depending on the Economic Department, the Emirates with which you choose to register your business and the trade name that you select.

    8. The value of trade name clearance and registration for new businesses

    Starting a new business is a daunting task. There are numerous tasks that a new company must complete in order to increase profitability and protect its developing assets. Selecting and securing all possible rights to your company name is a task that is frequently overlooked at the outset.

    Although most business owners recognize the importance of such protection, they frequently mistakenly believe a trade name registration in Dubai with the appropriate authority also secures trademark protection in the trade name they register. This is false: registering a trade name does not grant you trademark protection.

    They require a trade name search to determine whether you can use your trade name as a trademark. Because you cannot use or register a trademark that is likely to cause confusion with an existing mark, they use the search to determine whether or not someone else has used the same mark; this means that you need to find out is somebody else has the rights in the name you want to use.  

    You should conduct a trademark search on a national scale, going far beyond the limited search that the authority’s office may have conducted in granting your trade name. Although trademark searches are not perfect, they can help you determine whether your proposed mark has already been registered or is being used by someone else.

    If you proceed without conducting a search, you risk wasting time and money developing a trademark that you do not own and, worse, cannot use.

    9. Trade name registration in Dubai: The procedure

    You can do the trade name registration process online or offline. The following are some steps to take when registering a trade name:

    9.1. Choose a name based on the rules and regulations

    You should choose a trade name in accordance with applicable laws and regulations. DED shall have the authority to cancel any company name that does not comply with any of the following rules.

    9.1.1. The rules and regulations for choosing a company name

    • The business operation should reflect the company name.
    • A similar business in Dubai does not have a copyright to the company name.
    • You cannot include the term “indignity” in the trade’s name.
    • The trade name should not bear the name of God.
    • They do not recognize a few terms, such as Dubai’s Emirates, city names, districts, and airport codes.
    • You cannot use continent and country names in trade names, nationalities may be used as a name.
    • A company name cannot begin with European, Middle Eastern, Asian, or other names that have been translated.
    • There are no abbreviations for government agencies in a corporate name.
    • A company name cannot contain any popular global brands such as Apple, Samsung, Kia, and so on, either in part or entirely.
    • The company’s name contains no references to sectarian religious organizations or global political organizations, such as the FBI or the Vatican.
    • The division’s name cannot be the same as the parent company’s name, even if suffixes and legal names are not considered part of a name.
    • They do not allow using words like “ME” and “CO” for privately-owned businesses unless they are part of a phrase like “LCME Trading” or “ACTO Services.”
    • You should only use the first name, and at least one of the proposed shareholders must be named.
    • You should write titles literally and not translate, for example, if the Arabic name is « العاليــة الســماء», the trade name should be written as “Al Samaa Al Aalya”.

    9.2. Check the availability of the trade name

    After deciding on a name for your business, you must test the trade name availability in Dubai. You can check the availability using the public service of the Local Ministry of Economy.

What is a UAE Mainland business setup?

UAE Mainland company formation refers to the process of establishing and operating a business in the mainland area of the United Arab Emirates, outside of designated free zones. What is the process of obtaining a trade license in the UAE Mainland?

Obtaining a trade license in UAE Mainland typically involves several key steps. First, select a business activity and determine the appropriate legal form for your company. Next, choose and reserve a trade name that complies with the Department of Economic Development (DED) requirements and obtain initial approval. Following this, prepare the necessary documents, including the Memorandum of Association (MOA) and other legal agreements. Secure a physical office space that meets DED regulations. Finally, submit all required documents to the DED to obtain your trade license. By following these steps, you can ensure a smooth and efficient process for securing your trade license in the UAE Mainland.

What are the advantages of setting up a business in the UAE Mainland?

Some advantages of business setup in the UAE Mainland include access to a larger customer base, encompassing both the local UAE market and government entities. Are there any specific restrictions or regulations for certain business activities in the UAE Mainland?

What are the legal requirements for a business setup in UAE Mainland?

The legal requirements for UAE Mainland company formation may vary depending on the business activity and the jurisdiction.  However, common requirements include obtaining initial approval from the Department of Economic Development (DED), renting physical office space in accordance with DED guidelines, drafting a Memorandum of Association (MOA) and having it notarized, and submitting all required documents to obtain the necessary licenses.

What are the visa requirements for business owners and employees in the UAE Mainland?

The visa requirements for business owners and employees in the UAE Mainland include obtaining a residency visa, work permit, and Emirates ID. The exact requirements may vary depending on the business activity, company structure, and the nationality of the individuals involved.

Can a foreigner own a business in the UAE Mainland?

What are the taxation policies for a businesses operating in the UAE Mainland?

UAE Mainland businesses are subject to corporate tax, but the current rate is zero percent. However, there may be other taxes, such as Value Added Tax (VAT), which is applicable at a standard rate of 5% on eligible goods and services.

The common types of business entities in the UAE Mainland include Limited Liability Companies (LLC), Sole Proprietorships, Civil Companies, Branches of Foreign Companies, and Representative Offices.

    1. Designated Zones

    The designated zones in the UAE are VAT-free zones, which implies that when a company carries out any type of transfer of goods within or between designated zones, it will be exempt from VAT.

    1.1 Difference between Free zone and Designated zone.

    1.4  Businesses and supplies in a designated zone.

    Any organization or person carrying on economic activity in UAE and making taxable supplies will be registered for VAT purposes.

    Nevertheless, every company that registers in one of the designated VAT zones in UAE will have an economic model (supply and demand) different than a VAT registered organization.

    Although it is true that when a company carries out transactions in designated zones these are VAT-free. Not all have the same benefit, some supplies may attract 5%. In fact, the State will not tax only the supply of goods that meet certain conditions.

    2. Supply of goods within designated zones?

    The State considers outside the territory and subject to the payment of VAT all supplies of goods or tangible goods that are within one of the designated zones in the UAE.

    However, it should be noted that there are some cases in which this rule does not apply. As an example, to those who intend to use the goods within the area for private purposes and not to carry out any economic activity that includes transforming, reselling or manufacturing another good.

    The reason for this is that all goods purchased must be related to the goods produced for the State to consider them outside the scope of VAT. If seen from the financial point of view, they are more investment goods, so they must generate new economic activity.

    The following are some cases, thus facilitating the understanding of the subject.

    • All transactions of purchase and sale of goods for the purpose of resale.
    • If the company supplies the goods within the same designated zone to form part of another good and if the good is not consumed in another designated zone.
    • If the company supplies a good in one of the designated zones in the UAE to be used for the production of another good, provided that the good is not consumed within the same zone.

    2.1 Processes for the transfer of goods to a designated zone.

    General rules that apply to the transfer of goods to a Designated Zone prescribed in the United Arab Emirates Executive Regulation:

    • From outside the UAE to a Designated Zone: In this case, the companies move the goods from outside the UAE to another point outside the UAE. Therefore, they are outside the scope of VAT.
    • From the UAE mainland to a Designated Area: The government does not consider these types of cases as an export of goods from the UAE. Consequently, they analyze and tax these cases as making as a local supply.
    • Transfer of goods between Designated Zones: The government considers these types of transfers outside the scope of VAT. As long as the transfer of the goods between the respective designated zones is not altered. And the transaction complies with the rules established under the GCC Common Customs Law.

    2.2 Criteria you have to follow to supply goods free of VAT.

    • During the transfer between one of the designated zones in the UAE, the company should not deliver the goods.
    • Companies must comply with customs suspension regulations when transferring goods.
    • There must be no modification or use of the goods during the transfer.
    • The owners of the goods must provide a monetary guarantee if they do not meet the conditions for the supply of goods between designated zones in UAE.
    • Besides, 5% VAT is applied in the case of supplies of goods to and from the continental United Arab Emirates.

    2.3 For the importation of goods in Designated zones.

    When a company moves a good from a designated zone to the mainland. Then the State considers it as importation and taxes it as an importation.

    Nonetheless, some situations generate VAT on the purchase of goods within the designated zones in the UAE.

    Scenarios may occur such as when a company makes a purchase subject to VAT. And then during import from the designated zone to the mainland, it can regain the VAT payment. As long as there are no intermediate transactions during the purchase.

    This does not mean that the State cannot charge the VAT again in the event of a sale of the goods within the UAE Mainland and during the date of supply.

    3. How is the process for the VAT treatment of the supply of services within designated zones?

    When it comes to the provision of services within the designated zones. Then the government considers the place of supply of services to be inside the State of UAE. This means that they will provide and tax the service according to the regular VAT rules.

    In other words, it will not have concessional treatment within the designated zone.

    However, the State may consider the zero-rated transfer if the company exports the service from the designated area outside the GCC states.

    4. How is the process for the VAT treatment of water and energy supplies in designated zones?

    The state considers all water and energy supplies, ranging from electricity, water, and various types of gases, within designated zones in the UAE as supplies of goods. Meaning they are outside the scope of VAT as long as the company trades the goods within designated zones. Otherwise, they are subject to VAT.

How to Get An Investor Visa in Dubai

  • Published Date: May 26, 2025
  • Last Updated Date: July 29, 2025

Let's Chat



    How to get investor visa in Dubai? Dubai is indisputably one of the best places to do business in the world. As a major global business hub, many of the world’s most enterprising businesses converge there to do business. It is a way of bringing foreign talents into the country and allowing them to realize their business potential in one of the most important hubs on the planet.

    For rising entrepreneurs, the possibility of doing business in Dubai presents a major opportunity for growth. To get started, you will need to secure an investor visa. In the following sections, we will provide guidance on how to do this.

    What is a Dubai Investor Visa?

    The Dubai investor visa is designated for foreign citizens who live, work, and invest in Dubai. To obtain the visa, they must make a significant investment in Dubai. this usually takes the form of either real estate investment or starting a business.

    They are for two years and require at least AED 750,000 or AED 2 million for a golden one. Other emirates have similar procedures.

    Key Benefits of the Investor Visa

    Obtaining an investor visa provides a number of benefits. This includes the right to live in the UAE, the ability to sponsor family who also wish to live in Dubai, and access to the vast business network that Dubai provides.

    Who is Eligible for an Investor Visa in Dubai?

    There are specific categories of people who are eligible for the investor visa in Dubai, based on minimum capital requirements. This includes:

    • Business owners of an accredited business incubator, executive directors and entrepreneurs who meet minimum total investment requirements
    • Real estate owners who invest in properties worth at least AED 2 million
    • Partners and executive directors in either existing or new companies with a minimum total investment value of AED 2 million
    • Shareholders in UAE companies

    Types of Investor Visas in Dubai

    People who apply for investor visas in Dubai can get visas for different periods of time that will allow them a residence permit. The possibilities include:

    The 2-year investor visa. To be eligible, you must own property in Dubai with a value at least AED 750,000.

    You must be prepared to provide the necessary documentation, and also pass a medical examination, provide biometric data, and submit a certificate of good conduct.

    The 10-year golden visa. To be eligible for a golden visa, you should have at least AED 2 million in an investment fund inside Dubai, have an established company or be a partner of a company with a value of at least AED 2 million.

    If the applicant for a golden visa is an entrepreneur, he or she must also obtain approval from the Ministry of Economy for the golden visa.

    Real estate investor visa. The real estate investor visa is available to people who meet minimum requirements for different time periods. The 2-year type requires a minimum investment of AED 750,000 value in real estate.

    For 5 years, there is a minimum investment in property of AED 2 million. The 10-year golden visa also requires a property investment of AED 2 million.

    Step-by-Step Process to Get a Dubai Investor Visa

    In the sections below, we will describe the step-by-step process that you must go through to obtain an investor visa. You must meet the following conditions and procedures.

    Step 1 – Choose the Right Visa Type

    The first thing that you must do is decide what type of visa to apply for. Your decision should be based upon whether you apply for a real estate-based visa or an investor visa, as well as the amount of capital that you have to invest. This will also determine the amount of time that you receive your visa for.

    Step 2 – Register or Invest in a UAE Company / Property

    Once you have determined the type of visa that you want to apply for, the next step will be to register your business or startup, or invest in a UAE-based property.

    You must be able to prove your status to competent local authorities when you apply for your visa, so your investment should be fully completed by the time you submit your application.

    Step 3 – Obtain Necessary Documents

    Next, you should obtain the necessary documents to send in along with your application to send to the federal authority. There are several required documents that you must submit to obtain a visa. These include:

    • A copy of your original passport
    • A passport-sized photo
    • Your business license or the title deed from the property that you have invested in
    • Certain local banks statements that prove you have enough money to maintain your status in the country.
    • A copy of your Emirates ID

    Step 4 – Submit Application via ICP or GDRFA

    Once you have gathered all the required documents, you should submit your application either on the ICP website, or at the GDRFA.

    Step 5 – Undergo Medical & Emirates ID Process

    Your application will not be complete until you complete the following conditions: pass the required medical examination and obtain your Emirates ID.

    Required Documents for Dubai Investor Visa

    The required documents for the applicant are:

    • Your passport
    • A passport-sized photo
    • A copy of your business license or title deed for residence
    • Copies of bank statements
    • After you have submitted the application, a copy of your Emirates ID

    Costs and Fees for Investor Visa in Dubai

    There are fees that you must pay when applying for a visa to the Dubai Land Department. This includes:

    • Medical examination fee 
    • Emirates ID fee 
    • Confirmation of residency permit 
    • Dubai Land Department fee 
    • Administrative fee 
    • Legal and consultancy fees (optional)

    How Long Does the Visa Process Take?

    The average time that applicants must wait for their visa is 7-10 business days. There are some differences depending on the specific visa type and other circumstances in the applicant’s particular situation. If there are mistakes in the required documentation, or something is missing or incorrect then it will cause the process to be delayed.

    Can You Sponsor Family Members with Investor Visa?

    People who obtain a visa are able to sponsor members for residence Dubai. This includes spouses looking for a partner visa, children, and parents. The sponsor must meet minimum income requirements to be eligible for sponsorship, either having a monthly salary of AED 4000, or AED 3000 if accommodation is required). The sponsor will provide accommodation for the members that they host. Also, incoming members must pass a medical test and a criminal record test.

    The sponsor must provide proof of family relations for partner visas and other members to obtain residence. This includes birth certificates, marriage certificates, adoption certificates, documents required proving shared financial resources, and possibly other documentation. Fees are AED 7000 per member, and the applications must be sent within 60 days of members arriving in the country or there could be problems with the Dubai police to obtain a residence permit.

    Common Mistakes to Avoid During the Application

    There are several mistakes that people tend to make when applying for the Dubai investment visa. These include:

    • Sending incomplete documents. You should be sure to double-check the list of required documents and make sure everything is included. Not sending a complete application will cause delays.
    • Choosing the wrong visa type. Be sure that you read the details carefully of the visa type (golden visa or other type) that you are applying for and choose the one that matches your individual situation. If income requirements or other details are off, you will be rejected.
    • Ignoring local legal requirements. Be sure to familiarize yourself with all of the legal requirements for the visa you are applying for. It would be to your advantage to seek assistance in the application process.

    Final Thoughts: Is the Dubai Investor Visa Right for You?

    UAE offers the Dubai investor visa to obtain residency in the country for people with the right status. There are different categories of the visa – golden visa and shorter-term ones – so you should familiarize yourself with the terms and make sure you choose the right one.

    Seeking professional help from competent local authorities will help to clarify details and help ensure that you carry out the process correctly.

    Holding companies in Dubai are formed to organize and manage a group of smaller companies. If you are a business owner or investor, you may consider forming a holding company to protect your business assets or obtain a more favorable tax rate.

    In this article, we will explain in detail the steps to start a holding company. Keep reading to find out how to start a holding company in Dubai.

    1. Evaluate your business needs

    Holding companies in Dubai are incorporated companies that hold investments in other companies, called operating companies. The parent company does not engage in any business activities other than borrowing, lending, and making investment decisions.

    However, the holding company in Dubai lends funds or leases assets to an operating company that conducts business activity. The two most usual advantages of a holding business are tax decrease and asset safety.

    A holding company may provide a reduced tax rate by incorporating a state with a more favorable tax structure, or it may protect the company’s assets from losses to creditors of the operating company. Before starting a holding business, you should consider your commercial needs and the advantages you want to achieve.

    Holding companies in Dubai may also be suitable for a small business owner, as the holding company can provide asset protection for the high-value assets of the operating company. In this way, by forming a holding and operating company, a single person can protect their high-value personal and business assets from creditors of the company’s operations.

    2. Determine your business structure

    There are two predominant forms of a holding company in the UAE, the corporation and the Limited Liability Company or LLC. You should determine which form suits your needs, as the form you choose may affect your taxes and obligations.

    Most small business owners choose to form an LLC holding company, as the corporation structure generally does not provide the same asset protection. Consider what type of business you already have, if any, and what type of holding and operating company will suit your needs.

    If you are looking for a more favorable tax structure, you may want to consider forming your holding company in the UAE in a separate state from that of the operating company. You should consult a business expert to help you set up a business in another state.

    To maximize asset protection, you can form two LLCs, a holding company, and an operating company. You must create a separate entity for each, but the agent for each can be the same person: you. As long as you maintain the holding and operating companies as separate legal entities, the holding company will not be liable for the debts of the operating company.

    3. Submit a business application

    You will form your holding company in a Dubai free zone according to state laws and the type of business you want to form. Whether you form an LLC or a corporation, you will need to file with the state giving the business name, business agent name, and articles of incorporation for your business. You must do this for your operating company, as well as for your parent company if your operating company is not yet incorporated.

    Your articles of incorporation should state your company’s purpose and objective, the names of company officers, and how business decisions will be made. Update articles of incorporation as you make business changes.

    4. Create a specific bank account for your holding companies in Dubai

    To preserve individuality as separate businesses, the holding company and the working company must keep separate bank accounts and secretarial records. You should open a specific business account for your holding company by providing your new company tax ID when you create the account.

    5. Finance the holding company

    To start using the holding company, you need to finance the company to start investing in the operating company. The wealth from your companies should be stored in the holding company, and you can lend money to the operating company to fund operations as needed.

    If your operating company was already started before the parent company, start by selling all valuable assets of the operating company (such as land, buildings, large equipment, intellectual property, etc.) to the parent company by filing an asset transfer.

    6. Keep accounting records of your transactions

    As you operate your operating and portfolio companies, keep accurate accounting records of the transactions that take place between your businesses. Separate accounting records are essential to maintain the legal distinction between entities.

    The holding company must claim income for the amounts it obtains from the holding company as a lease or rental income, as long as that amount exceeds the expense of owning the asset. You need to keep records so that at the end of the year you can account for all the transfers that took place between your holding company and the operating companies.

    7. Perform all operational activities through the operating company

    Business activities are classified as operating, investing, or financing activities, and you must conduct all operating activities through your operating company, not through your parent company.

    Operating activities are the sale of goods and services that generate income in a business, such as the sale of groceries or clothing, or the sale of services such as dental work or carpet cleaning. To ensure that your holding company is never liable to creditors of the operating company, the holding company should never engage in these operating activities.

    The phrase “piercing the corporate veil” is commonly used to describe when a holding company is liable for the debts of an operating entity. This happens when the operations of the two companies are so intertwined that the holding company is responsible for paying the debts of the operating company.

    8. Invest and finance using the holding company

    The holding company may act as a lender or lessor to the operating company, whereby the holding company owns the company’s assets and the operating company rents them to the holding company.

    Each month, the operating company will pay lease expenses to the holding company, providing cash flow to the holding company. The holding company may also own the land and charge the operating company rent to use it, or lend the operating company money and collect interest payments.

    You should try to have most of the intercompany cash stored with the parent company. Where it can earn interest, and lend it to the operating company when needed. As long as the cash is in the accounts of the holding company, it is not subject to the liabilities of the operating company.

    Many holding companies invest in multiple businesses and owning shares in multiple businesses. Also, securing low interest using the financial security of diverse investments. The holding company earns income from the growth of investment in smaller companies. As well as any interest or lease income it earns.

What Is EMIRATES ID and How Can You Get It?

  • Published Date: May 26, 2025
  • Last Updated Date: July 29, 2025

Let's Chat



    If you plan to move to the Emirates, you will be required to have an Emirates ID. All residents and citizens of the country are required to have on. This is the primary identification document that you will need for all your official business in the country. Indeed, in pretty much every area of life, your card will be necessary, so it is essential that you obtain it when you move to the country.

    What is Emirates ID?

    Emirates ID is the main identity card that residents and citizens of the UAE use for conducting official personal activities in the country. On the ID, all your personal information is stored, including your biometric data, as well as a digital certificate.

    If you live in the Emirates, the Emirates ID is mandatory for traveling throughout the region, as well as for conducting any activity that involves government services, visiting healthcare providers, paying utility bills, and obtaining residency status. You also need it to vote.

    The Emirates ID is issued by the Federal Authority for Identity, Citizenship, Customs and Port Security (ICP).

    Who Needs an Emirates ID?

    There are different categories of people that must have the Emirates ID. This includes citizens of the country, foreigners residing in the country, and GCC nationals.

    • Citizens
    • Residents (including expats) who have a UAE residence visa
    • GCC Nationals residing in UAE

    Why is Emirates ID Important?

    Having an Emirates ID is important for many reasons. It serves many purposes related to government transactions, regional travel, healthcare, and access to local places. Renting property is not possible without official proof of your Emirates ID for UAE residents, and Emirates ID serves various other purposes, as well. Even registering for a SIM card is not possible without an Emirates ID.

    Key Uses of Emirates ID

    The ID ensures that you have access to the following facilities and services:

    • Access to all necessary government services 
    • Access to medical services and medical insurance 
    • A digital identity necessary for e-services and apps

    Emirates ID Card Features

    The Emirates ID has several distinct features. This includes:

    • Your full official name
    • Your nationality 
    • Your Emirates ID number
    • The chip that holds your biometric data
    • The validity and expiry date of your ID

    How to Apply for an Emirates ID

    We will now deceive the step-by-step process that you need to go through to obtain an Emirates ID. This applies to both residents and UAE citizens who do not yet have one.

    Step 1 – Obtain a Residency Visa (for Expats)

    For expats who have become residents of the country, they must first obtain a residency visa. There are different ways that people can do this, including gaining legal employment in the country, through family members that are UAE citizens or UAE residence visa holders, or by investing in the country.

    Step 2 – Submit Emirates ID Application

    The next step is to submit an Emirates ID application for an Emirates ID. This includes basic details that you will submit to judicial authorities that deal with foreigners affairs. You can either do this through the ICP website, or at one of the typing centers in the country. The application can be found online and includes clear instructions on how to complete it.

    Step 3 – Biometrics Appointment (if applicable)

    To obtain your ID, you will have to submit biometric data. This includes your fingerprints, as well as a photograph. It will be kept in the form of an electronic chip that includes your Emirates ID details and stores personal data. You can take care of both of these things at the ICP center.

    Step 4 – Wait for Approval & Card Delivery

    Once you submit your application form, you will have to wait between 7-10 days for it to be approved. You can then have it delivered to your address. You may be eligible for express service if you need urgent service for some reason.

    Required Documents for Emirates ID Application

    Along with your application form, there are several required documents with vital information that you must submit to the authorized authorities. While the requirements are specific to different categories of applicants, they include:

    • Your original passport 
    • For expats, a copy of your UAE residence visa
    • For children, a copy of their original birth certificate or their father’s birth certificate and Emirates ID card
    • A passport photo

    Emirates ID Fees & Validity

    Applicants must also pay fees along with their application form. This fee varies depending on which category the applicant falls into. 

    • For UAE nationals, the fee is AED 180 for five-year validity and AED 280 for ten-year validity 
    • For GCC nationals, the fee is AED 180 for five-year validity 
    • For foreigners with residency visas, the validity varies depending on the validity of their visas and the fee can also vary.

    These fees include the card issuance fee, service fee, and printing office fee. The financial transactions must be complete according to UAE regulations before various government services can be provided. If you need express service, pay the extra free for a hassle free experience. You can choose to receive an SMS notification once it is approved.

    Emirates ID Renewal Process

    At the end of the validity period, you will need to apply for renewal of your Emirates ID as your Emirates ID expires. Although you will have a 30-day grace period, you should be sure that you do not exceed it because you will be fined every day that you are late afterwards. Fines start at AED 20 per day and go up to AED 1000. 

    How to Track Emirates ID Status

    After you send in your application, you can track your status online. Just go to the ICP site and enter your application number (also known as PRAN) if you are a first-time applicant. If you are renewing or need a replacement, you can enter your existing Emirates ID number. The site will give you your status. Alternatively, you can request a status update via SMS.

    Lost or Damaged Emirates ID – What to Do?

    If your Emirates ID is lost or damaged, you should take swift measures to report it immediately. You don’t want to take the risk of someone using your card as their own. Go to the nearest police station to where the ID was lost and obtain a loss report.

    Also, you should go to the ICA site and list the ID as lost there, as well.

    Emirates ID for Children

    For children under the age of 15, parents or legal guardians need to apply for a card. This also applies to newborn babies. Without it, children won’t have access to medical care, travel privileges, or any other government services designated for residents and citizens.

    To obtain an ID for a child, parents need to submit a birth certificate or father’s passport and Emirates ID, as well as a passport photo.

    Final Tips & Common Mistakes to Avoid

    There are several basic but important things that you should keep in mind when you apply for an Emirates ID. Common mistakes in the application process include:

    • Typos in the application. If there are any errors in name spelling, dates, or other important material, the application will need to be submitted again.
    • Delays in renewal. It is easy to get complacent after you have received your first ID. Remember that there are consequences for delaying renewal, however.
    • Failure to keep contact information updated. If your mobile number or any other personal information changes, be sure that you have this changed in the system. A mismatch could cause you problems.

    If you are a citizen or resident of the Emirates, it is essential that you get an Emirates ID. Having an Emirates ID means accessing government services, medical care, insurance, having the ability to vote, being able to open a bank account and use banking credit cards, and many other essential services. Without this important national identity card, you will be stuck in terms of many of the things that you need. The process of obtaining an ID is not difficult, but you need to follow the steps carefully. And when your card expires, you need to make sure that you renew it on time to avoid having to pay costly fees. If you need help, you should employ the assistance of our professional service.

35 Best Side Hustles in Dubai to Earn Extra Money in the UAE

    As exciting as living in Dubai can be, we all know that it isn’t cheap. And in fact, the cost of living is going up all the time. If you feel like you aren’t making enough money to live comfortably, you might want to take on a side hustle. Taking on a side hustle can help you earn extra money and share your skills with others.

    More and more people are taking on extra jobs so that they can give themselves a financial boost and have more money at the end of the month. Many of these jobs require minimal investment and can provide substantial returns.

    In the sections below, we will describe 35 of the things that you can do to bring in extra cash. We have compiled these particular 35 ideas based upon extensive research into what are both the most popular gigs in the area, and the ones in highest demand.

    Looking at the population of Dubai, there is the largest crossover between people who have these skills, and potential beneficiaries that are willing to pay for them.

    Taking on a side hustle serves multiple purposes. There is a growing gig economy in the UAE because there are a lot of jobs that are necessary, but which are difficult to fill. Familiarizing yourself with what is out there and finding the right fit is key to success and figuring out how to earn extra money.

    Everything from digital marketing to online selling to language translation services can help you make money. You just have to figure out what works best for you.

    Economic Trends and Demand for Flexible Work

    As mentioned above, the cost of living in the country has been rising steadily. And people’s incomes are not necessarily going up at the same rate.

    In order to feel a sense of financial independence, people are looking beyond their regular jobs and taking on more side hustles to supplement their regular incomes. Whether you want to provide delivery services, share your cooking skills, or even work with pet care services, there is a great opportunity out there for you

    The freelance and gig economy in the UAE is booming. As more and more people find out about what is out there, the more popular these kinds of side hustles become.

    And the whole society stands to benefit as a result. Particularly if you have specialized services, you could well be in high demand.

    The process is being made easier by the fact that the digital transformation taking place (both globally and especially in Dubai) is making remote and online work more and more easy to find all the time. Many side hustles can be fulfilled simply by getting online and looking for online income.

    Legal Aspects – What You Need to Know

    There are certain things that you should know about taking on side hustles. You can’t just go out and grab one. There are legal considerations, and in many cases you will need to:

    Obtain a freelance permit, which costs between AED 7500 and 15,000. You can get this from the Ministry of Human Resources and Emiratisation. You might also need a trade license, depending on the type of work you pursue.

    Familiarize yourself with part-time work regulations. Part-time employees usually work between 20 and 30 hours a week, although this varies depending on the job. There are different rules for residents, expats, and sponsored individuals.

    And whether or not you have to meet particular time requirements depends on what you are doing. If you take on a freelance writing job, you may be able to work five hours a week to earn online income. It all depends, so you should familiarize yourself with the rules that apply to you.

    Learn about the different platforms available. There are several sites that offer gigs, including GoFreelance, TECOM, DED Trader License, and others.

    In some cases, it may be best to start a Facebook discussion page, or even utilize the community portal within your local community. It all depends on the type of work you want to do, your target demographic, and where potential customers tend to look for information.

    35 Best Side Hustle in Dubai to Earn Extra Money in 2025

    We will now provide an overview of the 35 best side hustles in Dubai that are popular these days. In some cases, you might be working with local businesses, in others, you will be able to make extra money and earn money online, and in some you might have to utilize freelance platforms.

    Some people prefer to work with small businesses, and others want to advertise their services online to make online money.

    Online & Digital Side Hustles

    There are several different online services to provide and digital side hustles that you can get that will help you earn money aside from your regular job. You may or may not need to sign an employment contract to earn online money, and in many cases – particularly for small businesses – you don’t.

    These side hustles are all Internet-based and don’t require leaving your home and will help you earn extra cash online as a form of income. They include:

    Freelance graphic design. Earning extra income from design can be a great side hustle for people with the right skills. Some graphic design jobs require a degree in design, but others don’t. If you have a knack for design and want to take on work in this area, put a portfolio together and look for gigs where you can utilize your talents.

    There are many startups in Dubai that are getting off the ground and could use help with their websites and other promotional material. Even the online gaming community needs designers. Look up job sites for creatives and see if you can find places that need help.

    Social media management. A lot of people need help in this area. You can get a side hustle that will help people create, schedule, and manage their social media content to optimize their followings and grow their social media while enabling you to earn money.

    Gig platforms will advertise people and groups that need help.

    Blogging or vlogging. Another gig that you can take on to earn money without signing an employment contract is blogging and vlogging. If you are a good writer and interested in content creation in web development, you might consider blogging about a subject of interest to you.

    Be sure that it is something that is of interest to people and will give you a significant following. Or, if you are good at making videos, you might try your hand at vlogging and video-based content creation for extra cash. Remember, though, that a lot of people are doing these things now, so you will have to work hard at it to monetize your efforts and earn money online.

    Dropshipping. Dropshipping is an order fulfilment option in which ecommerce companies outsource their procurement, shoring, and shipping duties to an external supplier.

    If this is something that interests you, create a portfolio on GoFreelance or one of the other platforms and advertise your services. If you have experience in this area, be sure to emphasize it on your page, and you can get extra money for it.

    Affiliate marketing. A lot of people are making extra money by taking on a side hustle in affiliate marketing, which is part of digital marketing. Many affiliate marketing companies are looking for people to advertise products and services through third-party sites.

    Payment takes place by the click, so every time someone clicks on a link, it results in a gain. In other words, it becomes a great source of passive income. You should have an interest in digital marketing and what kinds of messages work if you want to pursue this type of gig as a side hustle in Dubai.

    Virtual assistant. Another thing that many startups – and even more well-established businesses need is virtual assistants. You can gain extra cash with this kind of side hustle.

    Being a virtual assistant means that you can perform many of the functions that in-person assistants do, but from home. Communicating with customers, creating content for businesses, and handling other types of administrative tasks are all part of being a virtual assistant as a side hustle in Dubai.

    Copywriting and translation. If you are a good writer or have language skills, these can be useful for many Dubai-based companies and you can earn money through them. Copywriting is a side hustle that involves freelance writing articles for companies and using information available online as sources. Quality content creation is in great need.

    Many Dubai companies also need translators as they have international clientele. You can look on freelance sites or look up companies that work with certain countries that represent your language skills and contact them about possible translation work.

    Selling digital products. You can also sell e-books, templates, and other digital products in online marketplaces as a side hustle to generate revenue and earn money through. If you love reading and are good at summarizing and advertising books, this could be a good gig for you. Include this in your online portfolio, and include links to your work.

    In-Demand Skill-Based Gigs

    There are also quite a few skill-based gigs that could be good side hustles for you and help you earn extra money if you have the right skills. These include:

    Private tutoring. If you have in-depth knowledge of a particular subject or are interested in helping children with their academic needs, look online for private tutoring side hustles.

    There are a lot of families in Dubai with needs in this area, and you can pull in extra money by putting in after-school hours during your free time. This is a part time job that you can put in as many or few hours as you wish.

    Fitness coaching. Many people in Dubai want to take a break from their jobs and pay attention to their physical fitness.

    If you have a fitness-related skill, make yourself and your skills known at gyms in the area. Particularly if you have achievements or certification in fitness-related activities, you could be a good candidate to coach or teach classes for extra income with this kind of side hustle. It can be a great way to generate money and utilizing your extra time in a way that is useful and enjoyable for you.

    Event photography. Events are huge in Dubai. Like freelance writing, if you have photography skills, you could be in high demand to shoot events and make extra money with a photography side hustle. If you want to earn money in Dubai by freelancing in an industry that you know well, this is a great opportunity for freelancers.

    Especially if you have experience in this area, you should put together a site of your work and send it to events groups. Photographers can make very good money for their work, and the hours are flexible.

    Makeup services. If you want to earn money in Dubai outside your regular job, the city is a big spot for weddings and other kinds of formal events. Many women come there for destination events but are not sure where to go to get their makeup done. If you have makeup experience and want to earn extra income with it, go to www.mmgartists.com and advertise your services for a makeup side hustle. You should only consider doing this if you really know the professional techniques involved, though.

    Mobile car wash. You can get a side hustle providing car wash services to people who need them for extra income. Advertise online and make your presence known in your neighborhood. Maybe even put up physical signs so that people will notice them.

    Home catering/baking. Many people have events that they need caterers for, and you can earn extra income by starting up a home catering business and utilizing your cooking skills. You can shop at Dubai’s famous local markets for goods and use them to create your own specialties. The ability to cook homemade dishes Dubai is prized, indeed.

    For this kind of side hustle you will need a license, but it is possible to get one from the Dubai municipality. Start a social media presence for yourself by highlighting your selling homemade food and try to spread it around as widely as possible. You will soon find that you can earn additional money easily.

    App-Based & Gig Economy Jobs

    There is a growing market for app-based and gig economy side hustles in the area that will help you earn additional money. These are side hustles that don’t require a high skill level but which are nonetheless in high demand in the UAE. They include the following:

    Uber/Careem driver. Many people come to Dubai without their own forms of transportation. As public transportation is limited, there is a high demand for drivers.

    You will need to have an international driver’s license to get a side hustle with these companies and private vehicle registration. Drivers can make up to AED 10,000 per month.

    Talabat/Deliveroo delivery. Talabat and Deliveroo are two Dubai-based companies that provide delivery services.

    To get a side hustle with one of these companies, you need to be a legal adult and pass a basic background check. You also need to have an international driver’s license. Delivery workers can make up to AED 5000 per month.

    TaskRabbit jobs. If you are handy with home-related work, you might check out TaskRabbit-related side hustles. There are many kinds of home repair and renovation needs that people in the area have.

    If you have these skills, go onto the site and build a profile for yourself. Ask your first customers to leave reviews for you so that you can build your credibility. Income varies widely depending on the task.

    Pet sitting. Many people in Dubai travel frequently and need someone to take care of their pets while they are away. If you love animals, you can advertise your services at www.petwatchapp.com and get a job pet sitting. Dog walking services are a related activity that is prized by people who need it.

    As you build your credibility with customers, you will gain appeal as someone who can be trusted with people’s pets and build a solid side hustle this way. You might even become a pet’s favourite house sitter. Pet sitting/dog walking can make up to AED 30,000 a year.

    Grocery shopping. For people who are either too busy to do their own grocery shopping, or who are physically impaired, you can provide grocery services. Instacart, Fiverr, and even standard job sites like Indeed advertise these gigs. Personal shoppers can make up to AED 10,000 per month.

    Car sharing or renting. If you own a car, you may be able to make money off of car sharing as a reliable side hustle in Dubai.

    Creative & Passive Income Ideas

    There are other creative income ideas in which you can use your skills to help teach or entertain people in different ways as a side hustle in Dubai. They either involve working with small businesses, food businesses, other specialized services, online stores, or other profitable niches.

    Some of these ideas require more skills than others, but depending on your talents and interests, you might find one that is right for you.

    Print-on-demand. If you have the technological capability, you can provide print-on-demand services for companies that need things printed and don’t have the capacity themselves. People with events or special interest needs, for example, can be good candidates for clientele.

    To do this, you will need to start a formal company and register it, and you will have to obtain a license from the Department of Economic Development. If you decide to do this, it is best to focus on one or more particular niches (children’s birthday parties, for example) and advertise to these target audiences.

    Selling stock photos. If you are a serious photographer, you may be able to get involved in online selling and sell your photos to photo agencies in Dubai. Local laws require that you have a photo license, and that you comply with privacy laws established by the government.

    You will need to obtain either a freelance license or a business license. Be sure that you are familiar with the standards required by photo agencies for stock photos before you get started.

    Online courses. If you have a specialty area, you can share it with other people online in the form of an online course. To do this effectively, you will need to do research on what your precise topic of instruction should be and who else is offering courses on it.

    If your topic is already covered by a lot of people, you might not get many attendees in your courses. You will need to choose the right platform (Teachable and Udemy are popular ones, but you should make a decision based upon your specialty and your target audience. Qualifications vary depending on the particular platform that you choose.

    YouTube monetization. While it is a challenge to reach the point of monetizing a YouTube channel, it certainly isn’t impossible. As with teaching online courses, the trick is to find the right niche where you won’t have too much competition and can draw in a large enough audience to meet the requirements for the YouTube Partner Program.

    You will also need to have achieved a certain number of watch hours. Once you have met these criteria, you can start putting ads on your site, get fan funding, sell merchandise, and partner with other brands.

    REIT investment. Investing in real estate is becoming more and more popular globally. There are different ways to do it, and one of them is investing in a REIT (real estate investment trust). This is an excellent way to earn passive income while making just a minimal investment.

    REITs are companies that own income-producing real estate from which investors benefit when the REIT profits. To do this, you will need to open an account with a broker authorized to trade on NASDAQ Dubai.

    Niche blogging. If you have a specialty area that may be of interest to people, you could try niche blogging on one of several available online platforms. As with teaching and starting a YouTube channel, you will only be successful in monetizing your efforts if you choose a subject area that doesn’t have too much competition from other bloggers and which will draw a sufficient audience to make it worth your while.

    You can earn income from placing ads on your blog, selling products, or offering a premium account to people who want more in-depth information. You will also need to figure out how to reach your target audience, and this will depend on the subject area. Social media and subject-specific discussion forums are among the methods that people use.

    Each of these is a side hustle in Dubai worth pursuing for people with the right skills and interest.

    Local / Community-Based Side Hustles

    You can also take on hustles that involve your local community. Community-based side hustles vary depending on what type of community you live in and what the needs and interests of your neighbors are, but you can almost certainly find something that suits you.

    Organizing local events. Dubai is a place where things happen. Event organizing can vary from small-scale block parties to large-scale performance-type events and more. For some events, you might only need a permit to use a local park or venue.

    Others may be much more complicated. You should determine the needs of your local area and what type of event might suit people best.

    AirBnB hosting. This can be a great source of income in a place like Dubai, where hotel prices tend to be high and people want to look around for alternative places to stay. To do this, you need to comply with international AirBnB policies and find rental platforms on which you can advertise.

    In particular, you must be at least 18 years old, have a property that meets AirBnB standards, and be able to provide proof of identity and residence. You also need to have a valid bank account. Keep in mind that hosting can be a great source of income, but it also requires work. You will need to be able to handle problems that arise with your property and deal with any issues that arise with guests.

    Babysitting. A lot of people need babysitters when they want to go out and experience Dubai nightlife without the kids. Like babysitting anywhere, you will need to have a certain level of credibility with potential parents before they allow you to stay with their kids, but it can be a great side job with the neighbors.

    You can start by getting to know people in your community, and be prepared to provide references upon request. The more you are able to prove your experience with kids, the easier it will be to earn parents’ trust.

    House cleaning. House cleaning can also be a good way to earn money, although depending on your community, you might have stiff competition from immigrant guest workers that are willing to work for very little.

    Get to know the people in your community and make your desire to help known. You may be able to get people to choose you because they like and trust you and would like to give you the work, then you will be able to find flexible gig opportunities with several of your neighbors.

    Gardening/balcony services. Many people in Dubai own homes, but do not have time for gardening. If you have a green thumb, let the people in your community know it.

    If your community has an online discussion portal, make your services available publicly. You can even take the old-fashioned route and put up paper announcements on bulletin boards. This can be a fun side job if gardening is a hobby you enjoy.

    Handmade product sales. If you have a talent for crafts, whether they be pottery, crochet, or other kinds of things, you can try to sell them at community events. Being successful at this requires both the skill to make something that is unique and in sufficient demand, and also having good relations with others in your community.

    Tourist guide or translator. If you know the area well and have in-depth knowledge of both history and important sites, you might consider becoming a tourist guide. Look up tourist agencies in Dubai and send them your credentials.

    Particularly if you speak at least two languages, it might be a good gig for you. You might also find work as a translator, particularly if you speak languages that are needed in the area. Look up translation agencies in Dubai and send them your resume if this is of interest.

    Property management. If you have experience with property management, you can obtain a license from Dubai’s Real Estate Regulatory Agency and look for available jobs. You will need to undergo training and pass required exams.

    You will also need to obtain a trade license and register with the Dubai Department of Economy and Tourism. Dubai has websites that are devoted to jobs like this, such as Naukrifulf.

    Hosting language exchanges. As one of the world’s leading global hubs, Dubai is a potential mecca for language exchanges. There is a huge demand for language learning among businessmen and others in the area, and not everyone has the time for formal classes.

    Therefore, if you can find venues that will allow you to host language exchanges, you can advertise them online and try to attract the right mix of people who want to learn each other’s languages. You can charge a small fee for participation, and if you get the right number of participants then it could add up to a significant amount.

    How to Choose the Right Side Hustle for You

    If a lot of these ideas sound interesting but you’re not sure where to start, there are a few ways that you can determine what is best for you.

    First of all, think about what it is that you really enjoy. If you are taking on a side hustle in addition to your full time job, you will likely have already expended a lot of energy at the office. Therefore, taking on something else that is excessively difficult might drain you to the point of burnout. You might also need your employer’s consent.

    You also want to think about what you are good at, and whether or not people will really need your services.

    If you speak Swahili but this has no demand in the area, you might not get much of a response from translation agencies. If your community has a need for plumbers, but you’re only proficient with other types of renovations, this won’t be a good match either.

    The trick is to find the right combination of something that interests you and that is also in demand. And you will have to figure out how much you will make for the amount of time that you devote to the task. It should be enough to justify your efforts.

    To get the formula right, you will first need to familiarize yourself with what is out there and where the gaps are that you can potentially fill.

    Consider Your Time & Legal Status

    You will also need to figure out several practical things. First of all, you will need to determine whether you have the time for a side hustle. A lot of people think that it sounds like a good idea, but when it comes down to it they don’t actually have the time to do the job right. You will also need to consider your legal status. Not everyone is eligible for every type of job. If you are considering taking on a particular job, be sure that your residency or visa status allows for it.

    You will also want to consider whether your efforts will be scalable over time. If you start on a small scale and don’t make much initially, this is normal. But you want to be able to grow over time, unless you simply need quick cash in a pinch. Do your research on what the realistic earning potential is in your field.

    Start Small – Test Before You Invest

    Before you dive in head first, it is a good idea to start small and get a feel for what your gig will be like. Whether it be working in the food business, taking on translation services, working with content creation of different sorts, dog walking, web development/developing social media accounts, teaching online classes, pet house sitting, working with a dropshipping business, online gaming, or any number of other side jobs, you can start slowly and build up gradually. Try working with just a few test clients at first and see how successful you are, and how much you enjoy the work. Be sure to familiarize yourself with the platforms that will help you advertise best, such as Facebook groups and different kinds of marketplaces.

    There are different kinds of side hustle in Dubai. They include both online opportunities for people who have online content-related skills to offer, community-based opportunities for people looking to get more involved in their local communities, investment-related passive income possibilities, the opportunity to sell goods, and more. Finding the right side hustle means finding out what works best for you and the people who need your services. Who knows? You might find that something you once considered just a hobby like online gaming can actually bring in cash. Check out existing job portals and other online platforms and see what you can find. Advertise your services locally.

    You should be prepared to be flexible, yet still maintain focus on your primary task. Think about the growth potential of your potential gig and how much long-term success you expect to achieve. If you get the formula right, you could be in a great position to earn extra money and build your skills. So start thinking about what kind of side hustle in Dubai you might take on; you have nowhere to go but up.
