    4. The advantages of the UAE investor visa

    Starting your own business in Dubai and becoming an investor both have advantages. Here are some of the advantages of obtaining an investor visa in Dubai.

    • Residency: Because an investor visa is valid for three years, you are automatically eligible for a three-year Dubai residence visa.
    • Sponsor family: You can sponsor members of your immediate family to become UAE residents. Hence, your spouse, children, and parents are examples of immediate family members.
    • Travel Ease: If you have a Dubai investor visa, you can travel to any GCC country for business or pleasure. The investor status expedites the process of obtaining a travel visa to these areas. An employment visa does not provide the same level of convenience.
    • Outside country visa validity: With a Dubai investor visa, you can live outside the UAE for up to one (1) year at a time without having your residency revoked. However, this is not the case with dependent or employment visas. These visas only allow you to stay outside the UAE for a maximum of six (6) months. After this, they will revoke your UAE residence visa.
    • Long-term visa: Having an investor visa and establishing a successful business in the UAE can improve your chances of obtaining the UAE Golden Visa. The Golden Visa, a 10-year UAE residency visa is active since 2019. Its objective is to encourage business development and to reward investors and entrepreneurs for their contributions to the country’s economic growth.

    5. How can you obtain an Investor Visa in Dubai?

    5.1. Formation of a new company

    The simplest way to obtain an investor visa in Dubai is to register a company on the Dubai mainland. Depending on the legal structure of your business, when you form a company in Dubai, you become either the owner or a shareholder in the company.

    Hence, to apply for an investor visa, you must first establish your company.  Then, you have to submit the following documents to the Dubai immigration department:

    • Copies of trade licenses.
    • A copy of the legally attested company Memorandum of Association (for a partnership) or the Local Service Agent Agreement (for sole proprietorship)
    • Copy of the company’s business card.
    • Existing visa cancellation documentation (if you have an existing employment or Dubai residence visa you must cancel it).
    • If you have a visit or tourist visa, bring a copy of it with you.
    • On the other hand, the following steps are required to obtain your Dubai investor visa:
    • Getting your company registered with the Dubai Economic Department (DED).
    • Obtaining your company’s establishment card.
    • Applying for an entry permit to the UAE (if you are not already in the country), entering the UAE and changing your visa’s in-country status.
    • If you are already in the UAE, you can change your visa status in-country.
    • Carrying out your medical examination.
    • Obtaining your Emirates ID.
    • Obtaining adequate health insurance coverage.
    • Stamping your passport with an investor visa.

    5.1.1. Time required for processing

    From start to finish, the processing of your investor visa will take between 15-20 working days. This includes the time it takes:

    • Registering your new business in Dubai.
    • Obtaining your trade license.
    • Applying for a visa.
    • Having your investor visa stamped in your passport.

    5.2. Existing investment proof

    The other method of obtaining an investor visa in Dubai does not require the formation of a new company. It only requires you to show proof of your Dubai investments to the Dubai Municipality. Thus, if your request meets the UAE Government’s eligibility criteria, the Dubai Municipality will create your file with the Economic Department.

    Then, the Economic Department will issue you a reference file number, on which the Dubai Municipality will issue you a NOC (No Objection Certificate). Hence, to apply for your Dubai investor visa, you must present this NOC to the immigration department.

    • The amount invested must be a loan.
    • Financial stability of up to AED 10 million.

    7.2. Visa eligibility for 5 years

    You must meet the following requirements to obtain a 5-year investor visa in Dubai:

    • An investor must purchase a property worth at least AED 5 million.
    • This sum should not be obtained as a loan.
    • A minimum of three years is required for property retention.
    • The investor must purchase freehold property.

    7.3. Eligibility for a 3-year visa

    To be eligible for a 3-year investor visa in Dubai, you must meet the following requirements:

    • The investor must own property worth at least AED 750k.
    • If the property is mortgaged, the bank must be paid 50% of the total value upfront.
    • The investor must provide the bank with a no-objection letter written in Arabic.
    • The property can be divided among spouses, but the investor must provide a marriage certificate.
    • The property must be residential rather than commercial.
    • Also, the investor can apply through a jointly owned property if their share is valued at AED 750k or more.

UAE Labour Law: Your Go-To Guide for Work Rights

    In 2023, the UAE labour law underwent substantial revisions, ushering in a new era of employee and employer rights. These transformations are vital to understand fully, as they significantly impact your work life in the UAE. The UAE labour law 2023, represents a comprehensive framework designed to enhance the rights and protections of both employees and employers.

    In this article, we will unravel the new labour law UAE, offering insights into its new rights and responsibilities. We will see the essential changes, such as contractual rights, working hours, annual leave entitlements and even dispute resolution procedures. Whether you are an employee or an employer, this will serve as your reference for the 2023 UAE labour law.

    2023 UAE Labour Law Explained 

    The 2023 UAE labour law, represents a significant milestone in the evolution of labour regulations in the United Arab Emirates. This comprehensive legislation, also known as UAE law for employees, brings forth numerous updates and enhancements. Indeed, these updates aim to create a fair and balanced work environment.

    Firstly, under the labour law UAE, both employees and employers benefit from increased clarity and strengthened rights. This reform reflects the UAE government’s commitment to fostering a progressive and worker-friendly business landscape while ensuring that businesses can operate efficiently.

    Key provisions of the new UAE labour law address various aspects of employment. For instance, some of these aspects are contractual rights, working hours, annual leave, and end-of-service benefits. Overall, these changes empower employees with enhanced protections; such as timely salary payments, improved workplace safety standards, and swift access to end-of-service benefits upon termination.

    For employers, the new labour law UAE underscores specific obligations, emphasizing the importance of transparent employment contracts and safety regulations. This commitment to safeguarding worker rights and interests demonstrates the UAE’s dedication to maintaining a robust and equitable labour market.

    Key Updates for Employees

    The 2023 UAE labour law, often referred to as the new labour law in UAE 2023, introduces several pivotal changes. Certainly, these changes directly impact employees, enhancing their rights and protections under labour law UAE.

    However, before delving into specific sections of the new labour law, let us highlight some of the key updates. For instance, some of the most important changes that directly impact employees in the UAE are:

    Contractual Rights

    The 2023 UAE labour law prioritizes contractual rights to improve working conditions and safeguard employees’ interests. This, of course, in line with labour law UAE.

    This pivotal aspect of the UAE new labour law emphasizes the importance of written employment contracts. Employers are now mandated to provide detailed written contracts that outline the terms and conditions of employment. For instance, these conditions include but are not limited to salary, working hours, and job responsibilities. These contracts serve as a cornerstone in ensuring transparency and legal compliance.

    The introduction of clear and comprehensive employment contracts under the new labour law UAE is a significant milestone. Employees can now reference these contracts to assert their rights, knowing that their employment conditions are documented and legally binding.

    This move not only aligns with the new law of UAE for labour but also fosters a fair and equitable work environment. Thus, both employers and employees have a clear understanding of their rights and responsibilities. As such, contractual rights play a crucial role in upholding the principles of the new labour UAE 2023. Indeed, this ensures harmonious workplace relations in the United Arab Emirates.

    Working Hours and Overtime

    The new labour law in UAE 2023, has introduced significant changes in the realm of working hours and overtime. Overall, the changes align with the objectives of the labour law UAE.

    Under the UAE new labour law, the standard workweek is 48 hours, with a maximum of 8 hours per day. This sets a clear limit on regular working hours, ensuring that employees are not overburdened. Most importantly, any work conducted beyond these established limits is categorized as overtime. Of course, this entitles employees to additional compensation as stipulated in the new labour law UAE.

    The introduction of these specific working hour regulations demonstrates the commitment to safeguarding the well-being of employees in the United Arab Emirates. By enforcing such provisions, the new law of UAE for labour ensures that workers are not subjected to excessive workloads and are duly compensated for their extra efforts.

    In short, the provisions related to working hours and overtime in the new labour UAE 2023 create a more balanced and equitable work environment, where employees can enjoy reasonable working hours and fair compensation for additional efforts, fostering a harmonious employment landscape.

    Annual Leave and Holidays

    Under the provisions of the 2023 UAE labour law, annual leave and holidays have received significant attention, ensuring that employees enjoy their well-deserved time off while adhering to legal requirements. This section sheds light on the critical aspects of annual leave and holidays in the context of the new labour law.

    Employees in the UAE, as per the new UAE labour law, are entitled to annual leave based on their years of service. Generally, an employee with one to five years of service is granted 30 days of annual leave. Those with over five years of service receive 45 days of annual leave.

    Moreover, public holidays and religious holidays are now clearly defined and regulated under the new labour law. Employees are entitled to fully paid public holidays, such as New Year’s Day and National Day, in accordance with the UAE labour law 2023. Additionally, religious holidays like Eid Al Fitr and Eid Al Adha are also granted with full pay.

    It is essential to note that the new UAE labour law emphasizes equal treatment for all employees, irrespective of their nationality or religion. This ensures that everyone is entitled to these benefits, promoting a diverse and inclusive work environment.

    Employer Responsibilities

    In line with the comprehensive changes brought by the 2023 UAE labour law, employers bear significant responsibilities to ensure a fair and secure working environment. Understanding these obligations is paramount for fostering positive employer-employee relationships.

    Overall, some of the changes for employers that the new labour law UAE brings are:

    Payroll Rules

    The new UAE Labour Law 2023 has ushered in significant changes in payroll rules, impacting both employees and employers. The Labour Law UAE has strengthened payroll rules under its umbrella to promote transparency and safeguard employees’ financial rights. For instance, employers must now strictly adhere to these rules to avoid legal repercussions:

    • Salary Payments: According to the UAE labour law 2023, employers must pay salaries on time, preferably through bank transfers. This rule ensures prompt and secure salary disbursements, reducing the likelihood of delays or discrepancies.
    • Detailed Pay Slips: Employers must provide employees with detailed pay slips. These pay slips, as per the new Labour Law in UAE 2023, should contain a breakdown of salary components, including basic salary, allowances, and deductions. This transparency helps employees understand their compensation structure.
    • Overtime Compensation: The Labour Law UAE 2023 also addresses overtime compensation. Any work beyond the standard working hours, as outlined in the new Labour Law in UAE, must be compensated with additional pay. Employers have an obligation to accurately calculate and remit these payments.
    • Protection against Salary Deductions: The new UAE Labour Law 2023 reinforces strict rules against arbitrary salary deductions by employers. The law specifies deductions can only occur for specific reasons, such as employee misconduct or court orders.
    • Advance Notice for Salary Changes: Employers must provide employees with advance notice of any changes in their salary structures or benefits. This ensures that employees receive information and have time to adjust to these modifications, aligning with the principles of the UAE labour law for 2023.

    Safety at Work

    Under the provisions of the 2023 UAE Labour Law, “Safety at Work” has garnered significant attention. This aspect of the law underscores the UAE government’s commitment to ensuring the well-being of employees across the nation.

    Workplace safety, as delineated in the new UAE labour law, is a cornerstone for employees’ welfare. Employers must strictly adhere to these regulations, which encapsulate a wide array of aspects, such as ensuring hazard-free work environments, providing appropriate safety gear, and conducting regular safety training programs.

    The law necessitates that all workplaces, regardless of their nature or size, comply with stringent safety standards. This means employers must conduct risk assessments, implement preventive measures, and establish emergency protocols. By doing so, they create a safer work atmosphere that mitigates accidents and promotes employee well-being.

    Moreover, under the new labour law in UAE 2023, mandates that employers promptly report any workplace accidents. This reporting mechanism ensures that authorities can investigate incidents thoroughly, pinpoint the causes, and take necessary actions to prevent future occurrences.

    End-of-Service Benefits

    End-of-Service Benefits, a pivotal aspect of the 2023 UAE Labour Law, holds immense significance for employees. This provision reflects the commitment of the UAE government to safeguard the financial well-being of workers, making it a cornerstone of the new UAE labour law.

    According to the UAE labour law of 2023, they calculate these benefits based on an employee’s average daily wage. This significant change guarantees fair and equitable treatment for all employees, irrespective of their salary level.

    The UAE’s new labour law has designed this calculation methodology to offer a more accurate representation of an employee’s contributions to the workplace over time. It eliminates the potential for disparity in end-of-service benefits, making the process more transparent and fair.

    Employees can rest assured that the UAE law for employees mandates timely payment of these benefits. This financial safety net is a fundamental right, and employers must adhere to these regulations without exception.

    Handling Disputes

    In any workplace, disputes may arise. Understanding how to handle these conflicts is crucial for maintaining a harmonious work environment. Handling Disputes is a critical aspect of the 2023 UAE Labour Law, emphasizing the need for fair resolution mechanisms. The new UAE labour law recognizes that conflicts can arise in the workplace and aims to provide clear guidelines for addressing them.

    Resolving Conflict

    Resolving conflict is a pivotal aspect of the 2023 UAE Labour Law, which prioritizes amicable dispute resolution. The new UAE labour law underscores the importance of resolving conflicts fairly and efficiently to maintain workplace harmony.

    Under the new labour law in UAE 2023, mediation and negotiation are the preferred methods for addressing disputes. It encourages all parties to engage in open discussions and seek common ground. This approach fosters mutual understanding and often leads to more satisfactory resolutions.

    Documentation is key during the conflict resolution process as per the UAE new labour law. Keeping records of communication, meetings, and attempts at resolution is essential. This documentation can prove invaluable in case legal action becomes necessary.

    In instances where mediation and negotiation fail, employees retain the right to escalate the matter through the UAE labour court system, as outlined in the UAE law for employees. The new labour law of the UAE aims to expedite the legal process, ensuring it addresses disputes promptly and equitably.

    Legal Options

    Legal options available under the 2023 UAE Labour Law serve as a safeguard for employees’ rights. This vital component of the new UAE labour law outlines the steps employees can take when all else fails.

    In cases where mediation and negotiation cannot resolve disputes, the UAE labour court system becomes an alternative as per the UAE new labour law. Employees have the right to seek legal redress, ensuring they protect their interests.

    The new labour law in UAE 2023 aims to streamline these legal processes. It ensures that it promptly addresses disputes, expedites the resolution, and minimizes the stress and uncertainty often associated with lengthy legal battles.

    Under the UAE law for employees, this legal avenue is a fundamental right. It reinforces the principle that employees deserve a fair and just workplace, aligning with the broader goals of the new law of UAE for labour.

    In summary, legal options provided by the new labour UAE 2023 offer a vital means of recourse for employees facing unresolved disputes. By understanding these regulations, employees can navigate the legal system with confidence, promoting a workplace environment characterized by justice and accountability.

    Conclusion: Your Rights under UAE Labour Law 2023

    In conclusion, the UAE labour law 2023 represents a significant stride towards safeguarding employee rights. With its emphasis on contractual clarity, workplace safety, and efficient dispute resolution, it sets the stage for a fair and harmonious working environment.

    Both employees and employers must acquaint themselves with these regulations to ensure compliance and contribute to a prosperous and equitable workplace. By doing so, they align with the broader goals of the new labour law in UAE 2023, fostering a climate where rights are respected, disputes are resolved justly, and the well-being of all parties is prioritized.

UAE Ministry of Labour Employee Benefits & Welfare Programs

  • Published Date: February 22, 2025
  • Last Updated Date: July 29, 2025

Let's Chat



    The United Arab Emirates (UAE) is a country that offers several benefits and welfare programs to its workers. Among these benefits are competitive salaries, paid vacations, health insurance, and severance pay, among others. The Ministry of Labour UAE is the body whose purpose is to regulate and supervise these programs and benefits. In addition, it protects the rights of workers and employers.

    In this article, we are going to explore the main benefits and wellness programs that exist in the UAE. Specifically, for workers, both foreign and national. We will also see how the Ministry of Labour UAE ensures compliance with labor laws and resolves disputes that may arise between the parties. Finally, we will analyze the opportunities and challenges facing the labor sector in the UAE in the current context.

    Understanding Employee Benefits in the UAE

    Employee benefits are those provided to you by your organization in addition to your salary or predetermined salary. Furthermore, these benefits can take the form of monetary or non-monetary features. In this way, they can improve the overall compensation that employees receive. Among the most common examples of employee benefits, we find:

    • A provident fund for employees.
    • Health insurance.
    • Statutory permits.
    • Leave for maternity and paternity leave.
    • Different subsidies, such as transportation subsidies.
    • Bonus for one year of service.
    • Refunds for bills such as internet, mobile, etc.

    Federal law decree number 33 of 2021 is the main law that regulates the UAE labor laws and their correlative executive regulations. In addition, all other ministerial orders that implement all these provisions. In this way, the laws are responsible for regulating all relationships between employees and their employers.

    Knowing employment rights is essential and also for those who apply the laws. However, these laws apply to all national and international workers except for:

    • Workers and officials of local and federal governments.
    • The armed forces, security agents, and police.
    • Those workers who are subject to the Employment Law number of the DIFC. In addition, workers who are subject to the ADGM Employment Regulations of 2019.

    These laws are responsible for protecting employees from any wrongful termination of their employment. Additionally, it guides employers on minimum wage standards, employee benefits, and compensation. Also retirement plans and other matters related to employment.

    Overview of UAE Ministry of Labour

    The MOL UAE is responsible for supervising the entire workforce. In addition, it regulates the entire employment process in the private and public sectors. In this way, its mission is not only to enforce labor laws but also to foster a harmonious work environment. MOL UAE’s operations demonstrate its commitment to safeguarding the rights and interests of employees and employers.

    Therefore, it plays the role of maintaining the balance of the employment landscape in the United Arab Emirates. In this way, it strives to defend the principles of justice, compliance, and equity of labor laws and regulations. For this reason, it guarantees that national and foreign employers enjoy the same protection.

    In order to fulfill this mission, MOL UAE offers channels such as the MOL UAE consultation and a toll-free number for labor complaints. In this way, workers can express all their concerns and find a solution. Among the objectives of the MOL UAE, we find:

    • Regulations of labor practices.
    • Guarantee the protection of all workers.
    • Promote sustainable employment.
    • Streamline all business operations.
    • Labor inspections.

    Mandatory Employee Benefits in the UAE

    Among the things you have to learn before opening a business in Dubai are mandatory employee benefits. Below, you will see all the benefits imposed by the Ministry of Labour UAE for workers.

    Minimum wage: In essence, there is no universal minimum wage or mandatory wage for foreigners in the UAE. On the other hand, nationals have a minimum salary according to their university degree, that is:

    • Graduation less than high school: AED 3,000 per month
    • High school graduation: AED 4,000 per month.
    • University certificate: AED 5,000 per month.

    Payroll cycle: The payroll cycle in Dubai and the other emirates is monthly.

    13th Salary: There is no rule about offering the 13th salary in the UAE.

    Working hours: In the UAE the working hours are 48 hours per week. That is 8 hours a day. But, for public sector employees, university and school work weeks are 4 days and hours. For instance, if an employee makes a job relocation, they also have to follow this work schedule.

    On the other hand, employees have one or more breaks during the work day. Specifically, if the job lasts more than five hours.

    Overtime: An employer may ask you to work overtime. If this is your situation, you have to know that it cannot be more than two hours a day and they must be paid the corresponding remuneration. For instance, on normal days, the remuneration per extra hour will be at a rate of 125%.

    Minimum number of leaves in a year: Depending on the compensation structure in the UAE, there are leave policies in place. Leave benefits in the UAE require that employees be eligible for a minimum of 30 days of paid leave. In addition, holidays such as UAE National Day are additional to these mandatory licenses.

    Additional Welfare Programs by the Ministry of Labour

    In addition to the mandatory employee benefits, an employer may choose to offer some additional benefits. The idea of ​​these additional benefits is to try to retain workers in the companies. For instance, life insurance, additional vacations, flexible work schedules, family health insurance, and flexible work schedules can be offered. Below you will see a brief description of some of these complementary benefits.

    Flexible work schedules: The purpose of this policy is to give employees the freedom to work from wherever and whenever they want. As a result, employees can maintain work-life balance and enjoy work. Additionally, with this, you can increase employee loyalty to the company.

    Additional Holidays: Offering additional leaves and holidays to employees can be an added benefit. Having to work for 8 or 9 hours a day continuously can be exhausting for employees. That’s why an extra vacation is an excellent opportunity to catch up with family and friends.

    Workshops and training: Free courses and workshops are additional benefits for employees. Especially for those who want to learn and develop their skills. The idea is to help them improve their professional prospects. As an employer, you can offer free courses to workers and show interest in their personal development.

    Health Insurance: Additional health benefits for your families and employees can be great additional benefits. A good option is to give gym memberships, health insurance, or other types of health benefits.

    Rights and Protection of Employees under Law

    The Ministry of Labour UAE also establishes the labor rights of employees. Simply put, workers’ rights are laws to ensure their protection. Specifically, on the intellectual and financial rights of employees. In addition, to obtain full rights in exchange for their work and to protect them from deception and fraud. The most important rights of employees in the UAE are the following:

    Employment contract: All employees in the UAE must have a written employment contract. It must describe the terms and conditions of employment. For example, working hours, salary, leave entitlements, and notice period. An interesting fact is that this is one of the most important rights of workers.

    Working hours: In the UAE, the standard working day is 8 hours per day or 48 hours per week. However, you have to know that during Ramadan or in some industries, the working day may be shorter.

    Overtime: If a worker works longer than their normal working day, they must receive overtime pay. This is approximately 25% or 50% of your regular hourly wage.

    Annual Leave: Employees may take annual leave upon completing one year of continuous service. These vacations are a minimum of 30 calendar days for employees with less than 5 years in the company. However, employees with more than 5 years in the company can enjoy annual leave for 45 calendar days.

    Sick leave: Employees can take sick leave at full pay for a maximum of 90 days a year. To do this, you have to present a medical certificate from an authorized doctor.

    Maternity leave: Employees may take maternity leave for a period of 45 days with full pay. You have to know that this time includes both the prenatal and postnatal periods. Additionally, this can be extended up to 100 days if a complication occurs.

    Impact on Employee Retention and Satisfaction

    Currently, in the UAE there is a dynamic and fast business environment. This is why job satisfaction plays a crucial role in the productivity and general well-being of employees. It is essential to understand the factors that are part of job satisfaction.

    You have to know that all the benefits mandated by the Ministry of Labor UAE have an impact on employees. Specifically, in the form of satisfaction and retention. Below, you will see the description of the factors that are part of this impact or job satisfaction that employees enjoy.

    Positive and welcoming work environment: A positive work environment must exist in the company; specifically, between employees or departments. In the UAE, companies prioritize providing a supportive or inclusive work culture. Additionally, the importance of collaboration, teamwork, and mutual respect is emphasized. In other words, everything that contributes to a harmonious work environment. This is why organizations in the country usually invest in employee well-being programs.

    Rewards and Recognition: Rewarding and recognizing employee contributions and achievements is a critical factor in increasing employee satisfaction.     A Step-by-Step Guide to Visa Cancellation in the UAE:

    The process of how to cancel visa in UAE involves certain steps. Not completing a step will result in delays.

    Step 1: Obtain a No Objection Certificate:

    The first step for expat employees is to get an NOC from their employer. It indicates your employer has no issues with you canceling your visa.

    Step 2: Apply for Visa Cancellation:

    Apply through GDRFA for visa cancellation. If you are in free zone, apply with the respective authority. Usually employers will be the ones managing this process. But freelancers have it upon themselves to take care of this step.

    Step 3: Settle Fines or Outstanding Debts:

    Before visa cancellation is processed, clear any impending fines and penalties.

    Step 4: Submit Documentation:

    Share the following documents.

    • Your Original Passport.
    • Visa Copy.
    • Emirates ID.
    • Company’s Cancellation Form.

    Common Mistakes to Avoid During Visa Cancellation in the UAE:

    There are different causes for delays and fines occurring. Most of the times, it’s some common mistakes most people make. It turns the simple process into a complicated thing. Avoiding these ensures a smooth process ahead.

    Failing to Settle Debts Unpaid bills and traffic fines are common contenders blocking your visa cancellation
    Missing Deadlines If your employment has been terminated, cancel your visa in the specific timeframe
    Lack of Proper Documentation Avoid running into setbacks by making sure you have all the required documents

     

    How to Cancel Your UAE Visa While Outside the Country?

    You can cancel your visa when you are out of the country. This is how it works when you have left UAE.

    Contact Your Employer or Sponsor:

    Companies and sponsors manage the process for employed individuals. Freelancers need to contact their free zone or GDFRFA.

    Submit a Power of Attorney:

    Assign a representative to handle the paperwork on your behalf. This requires power of attorney document.

    Clear Any Pending Fees:

    Clear any unpaid fines before the visa can be canceled.

    Receive Confirmation:

    After all procedures are completed, you’ll receive a notification. It will inform you of official visa cancellation.

    Visa Cancellation vs. Visa Expiry: What’s the Difference in the UAE?

    Knowing the difference between visa cancellation and visa expiry is important for expats. The terms may sound similar. But they point to different situations with distinct consequences.

    Cancellation Expiry
    It is initiated by either the sponsor, employer or individual, A visa naturally expires when it reaches the end of its validity period,
    This is necessary for people leaving a job. Or the country. Or if they are switching to a new visa type. Overstaying on an expired visa is a recipe for heavy fines.

    What Happens After Your UAE Visa is Canceled: Next Steps for Expats?

    There’s a grace period of thirty days to leave the country when your visa has been canceled. Or this time can be used to apply for a new visa. During this window, settle final bills. Cancel utilities. Close any bank accounts if you are not planning on returning.

    UAE lets you apply for a visit visa to extend your stay temporarily. Meanwhile you consider your next steps.

     

    UAE Employment Visa Cancellation: Employer and Employee Responsibilities:

    The process of canceling an employment visa in the UAE is a shared responsibility between the employer and the employee.

    • Employer Responsibilities:
      Start the cancellation process with the MoHRE and GDRFA.
    • Employee Responsibilities:
      Provide required documents. Pay any outstanding dues. Return their Emirates ID and work permit.

     

    Freelance Visa Cancellation in the UAE: What You Need to Know?

    Freelancers are their own sponsors. This gives them a bit more control over the process. But it comes with added responsibility. There are certain steps freelancers in UAE have to follow for canceling their visa.

    Contact the Free Zone Authority:

    If you’re registered under a free zone, start the visa cancellation with the authority that issued your freelance permit.

    Submit Your Documents:

    Required documents include your passport, visa copy, Emirates ID and a completed cancellation form.

    Settle Any Dues:

    Ensure that there are no pending fines before submitting your cancellation request.

    Visa Cancellation Fees in the UAE: What to Expect in 2025?

    There’s no such thing that comes without a cost. And visa cancellation is no exception for that matter. Be if an employment or freelance visa you are cancelling, the total amount will differ. That’s because of your visa type, location and fines. Visa cancellation will cost you between AED 200 to AED 500.

    There might be administrative fee applied too. Get in touch with relevant government authorities. Or contact your sponsor. They will get you an accurate estimate of cancellation expenses.

    How Visa Cancellation Affects Dependents in the UAE?

    When main visa holder cancels their visa, it will affect their dependents too. The dependents’ visas need to be canceled too. But similar to the primary visa holder, they also get a 30 day grace period. Primary visa holder will have to initiate dependent visa cancellation process.
    Not cancelling your dependents’ visas in time will mean fines. And even difficulties in securing new visas for your family in the future.

     

    Can You Get a New Job After Canceling Your UAE Visa? What You Need to Know?

    It’s possible to get a new job after canceling your visa. After your prior employment visa is canceled, you can apply for a new job in the country. Your new employer will sponsor your visa when you are hired elsewhere. Transfer process for switching employers in the same free zone is even simpler. It might not require you going through a full visa cancellation either.

    Introduction to the UAE Establishment Card

    What is establishment card? It is an official document issued by the UAE Authorities of the jurisdiction where you have incorporated your company.

    Thus, it serves as proof that your business is legally allowed to carry out its operations in the UAE where it has been registered. For this reason, companies have to get this document to demonstrate it is authorized to work.

    The following is what this document contains:

    • Name of the company
    • Card number
    • Expiry date

    Additionally, this document is also known by other names or terms, such as the following:

    • Establishment immigration card
    • Establishment labor card
    • Company Establishment Card, or CEC
    • Corporation Immigration Card, or CIC

    It is important to point out that an establishment card is different from a business license in the UAE. Therefore, these are not the same document but both are necessary for running your business in the UAE.

    Why an UAE Establishment Card Is Essential for Your Business Success

    An establishment card is a must if you want to set up your presence in the UAE. Whether you want to launch an import and export business in Dubai or any other type of company, you should obtain this document too.

    The following are the reasons why you need to have this document:

    • Proof of operation: as we have mentioned before, it serves as proof of authorized operations in the UAE. So, you can prove your company is legal and registered.

    Therefore, you have to know who is the UAE Authority in charge of issuing your license and other business documents.

    Whether you are applying for an establishment card Dubai or in any other Emirate, you have to know that the registration authority is not the one that issues this document.

    The following are the responsible for issuing the establishment card:

    • If your business is registered in Dubai, the General Directorate of Residency and Foreigners Affairs Dubai (GDRFAD) is in charge of issuing it.
    • If your business is registered in any other Emirate, the Federal Authority for Identity, Citizenship, Customs & Port Security (ICP) is in charge of issuing it.

    • In the case of a manager, a copy of an authorization by the Notary Public

    In this article, you will learn everything about a Free Zone Visa. There are numerous advantages you can enjoy with this type of travel permit. Let us look at a more detailed explanation of:

    1. Dubai Free Zone Visa: Rules and regulations

    • It is easier to obtain a Free Zone Residence Visa if you work for a free zone company. The visa is only valid for three years.
    • If you are an entrepreneur looking to establish a business in the UAE, you can apply for either an Employment visa or an Investor visa. Once you have obtained an Investor or Employment Visa, your dependents can apply for a residence visa. The visa is valid for three years.
    • Free Zone Visas are issued by the Immigration Department (GDRFA) without the need to contact the Ministry of Labor. These visas are relatively easy to obtain; however, visa holders are not permitted to work outside free zones. To obtain work permits, you can apply for a NOC from the Ministry of Labor.

    2. The advantages of having a UAE Free Zone Visa

    Investors and entrepreneurs can successfully operate their businesses in the UAE through free zones, which also provide residency and operational flexibility. If a foreign company applies for a visa, it will receive the following benefits:

    2.1. Exemption from paying taxes

    Firstly, you are not required to pay any import, export, or personal taxes if you have a Free Zone Visa. Organizations are also exempt from paying corporate taxes for a set period, which can be renewed at a later date.

    2.2. Complete ownership

    The UAE’s government, in 2018, approved a law that allows foreign investors and entrepreneurs to gain 100% ownership of their company without the need for an Emirati shareholder. As a result, they would be able to maintain complete control of the company.

    2.3. Financial access that is efficient

    With a UAE Residence Visa, you are immediately eligible to open a bank account, transfer funds, and engage in any financial services. 

    2.4. Rent corporate space

    You can rent office space and other properties based on your requirements. There is an advantage to choosing long-term leasing options that can last up to 25 years.

    2.5. Healthcare accessibility

    Lastly, residents with a UAE Free Zone Visa will be eligible to apply for an Emirates ID and will have access to the same healthcare services as UAE residents. This includes selecting a low-cost health insurance policy.

    3. Step-by-step guide to obtaining a Free Zone Visa in Dubai

    When you apply for your Free Zone Visa in Dubai with us, we will walk you through the five steps below.

    3.1. Sign up for e-commerce services

    Because the Free Zone Visa application is mostly done online, you must first register with the UAE government’s e-channel portal. All that is required in the mandatory registration fee of AED 2,500 is for Connect Services Middle East to manage this process for you.

    3.2. A permit to enter

    After you have completed your initial registration, you can apply for your entry permit. This is similar to a temporary visa in that you can enter and stay in the UAE for up to 60 days. While you are permitted to leave during this time, it is strongly advised that you do not because it may cause problems with your immigration file.

    3.3. A change in status

    Thirdly, the status change comes next. This is how you activate your entry permit. You can do this by submitting your passport to immigration in the UAE for stamping, presenting your visa to immigration at an airport when entering the UAE, or leaving the UAE by land and having your permit stamped upon re-entry.

    The former is by far the most straightforward option.

    3.4. Registration for medical services and Emirates ID

    A medical exam and a fitness test are required to obtain a Free Zone Visa. This includes a blood test as well as a chest X-ray. Once you have your test results, you can apply for your Emirates ID, which will grant you access to services in the UAE.

    3.5. Stamping of a residence visa

    Finally, you need to insert the actual Residence Visa into your passport. This can be accomplished by presenting your passport to the relevant immigration authority in the UAE. Once this stage is completed, you will be able to live and work in Dubai until your visa expires.

How to Calculate Overtime in Saudi Arabia (KSA)

    Overtime calculation in Saudi Arabia is an important responsibility for employers, payroll teams, and HR managers. At the same time, employees should also understand how their extra working hours are paid. Knowing the correct overtime formula ensures compliance with Saudi Labor Law and builds trust between companies and workers.
    Looking for expert help with compliance and payroll management in Saudi Arabia? Contact us today to streamline your HR and payroll processes.

    Standard Working Hours in Saudi Arabia

    According to Article 98 of the Saudi Labor Law:

    • Standard working hours are 8 hours per day or 48 hours per week.
    • During Ramadan, working hours for Muslim employees are reduced to 6 hours per day or 36 hours per week.
    • Daily working hours include rest, prayer, and meal breaks, provided they do not exceed 30 minutes per break.

    Who is Eligible for Overtime in KSA?

    Most employees in Saudi Arabia are entitled to overtime pay. However, there are a few exceptions:

    • Senior managerial or supervisory positions with decision-making authority.
    • Certain workers such as guards or janitors under specific labor contracts.
    • Roles where flexible hours are already part of the compensation package.

     

    If you are working in Saudi under an employment visa, your contract should clearly mention working hours and overtime eligibility.
    Tip for Employers: Ensure all contracts are legally compliant to avoid disputes. Need assistance? Our team provides PRO services in Saudi Arabia to help you handle legal requirements smoothly.

    Overtime Pay Formula in Saudi Arabia

    The official overtime formula under Saudi labor law is:
    Overtime Pay = Hourly Rate × 1.5 × Overtime Hours
    Where:

    • Hourly Rate = Monthly Salary ÷ 30 ÷ 8
    • 1.5 = Overtime multiplier (150% of the normal hourly wage)

     

    Employers using payroll outsourcing services can automate this formula to ensure accuracy and compliance.
    Save time and reduce errors check out our HR outsourcing services for complete payroll and overtime management solutions.

    Overtime on Weekends and Public Holidays

    If employees work on weekends or public holidays, the same 1.5x multiplier applies. Employers must also provide a substitute rest day if the employee’s weekly day off is not respected.

    Step-by-Step Overtime Calculation Example

    Example 1: Monthly Salary Employee

    • Monthly Salary: SAR 6,000
    •  Hourly Rate = 6,000 ÷ 30 ÷ 8 = SAR 25/hour
    • Overtime Hours Worked: 10 hours
    •  Overtime Pay = 25 × 1.5 × 10 = SAR 375

    Example 2: Hourly Wage Employee

    • Hourly Rate: SAR 20
    • Overtime Hours Worked: 15 hours
    • Overtime Pay = 20 × 1.5 × 15 = SAR 450

    Maximum Overtime Limits

    • Total working hours (including overtime) must not exceed 11 hours per day.
    • Weekly overtime should not exceed legal limits set by the Ministry of Human Resources and Social Development (MHRSD).
    • Employers should obtain employee consent for overtime beyond standard shifts.

    Compliance & Best Practices for Employers

    • Maintain accurate attendance and timesheet records.
    • Use HR outsourcing services in UAE to streamline compliance.
    • Clearly state overtime policies in employee contracts.
    • Pay overtime in the same payroll cycle to avoid disputes.

     

    Struggling to manage compliance? Our experts can guide you with payroll, HR, and labor law advisory. Book a free consultation today.

    Employee Rights in Overtime

    Employees can raise disputes through the Saudi Ministry of HR & Social Development (MHRSD) if overtime pay is not provided.
    Employers may face fines and penalties for failing to comply with labor laws.
    Overtime pay is generally included in wage calculations for GOSI (social insurance) contributions.
    For assistance in filing disputes or document processing, you can rely on PRO services in Saudi Arabia.

    Saudi Arabia vs Other GCC Countries

    Country Standard Hours Overtime Rate Ramadan Hours
    Saudi Arabia 8/day, 48/week 1.5× hourly rate 6/day, 36/week
    UAE  8/day, 48/week 1.25–1.5× depending on time 6/day
    Qatar  8/day, 48/week 1.25–1.5× 6/day
    Oman   9/day, 45/week 1.25–1.5× 6/day

    Frequently Asked Questions (FAQs)

    Q1. What is the legal overtime rate in Saudi Arabia?
    The overtime rate is 1.5 times the hourly wage for each extra hour worked beyond standard hours.

    Q2. Do employees get overtime during Ramadan?
    Yes. If employees work beyond the reduced Ramadan hours (6 hours/day), they must be compensated at the overtime rate.

    Q3. Is overtime paid on weekends and public holidays?
    Yes. Work performed on weekends or holidays must be compensated at the 150% overtime rate.

    Q4. Are managers entitled to overtime in KSA?
    Not always. Senior managers and supervisory staff with authority over others may be exempt from overtime under Article 108.

    Q5. What is the maximum overtime allowed per day?
    Working hours including overtime cannot exceed 11 hours in a single day.

    Q6. How do you calculate fractional overtime (e.g., 30 minutes)?
    Convert minutes into a decimal (30 minutes = 0.5 hour) and apply the standard formula.

    Q7. Can employees refuse overtime?
    Employees may refuse overtime beyond legal limits unless their contract explicitly requires flexibility.

    Q8. How to claim unpaid overtime in Saudi Arabia?
    Employees can file a complaint with the Labor Office (MHRSD). Employers may be fined or required to pay back wages.

    Conclusion

    Understanding overtime calculation in Saudi Arabia is essential for both employers and employees. By following the official formula, respecting maximum limits, and keeping accurate records, businesses can remain compliant with Saudi labor laws while ensuring employees are fairly compensated for their extra efforts.

    To determine if becoming a landlord would benefit you, calculate your cash flow by calculating your initial and continuing expenditures against your predicted rental revenue.     Market rental options

    The 50 percent rule states that the total running expenditures for a rental property should be about 50 percent of the revenue.

    Mortgage principal and interest are not included in operating expenditures. The remaining 50% may be utilized to make the monthly mortgage payment. You may use this to rapidly estimate an investment’s cash flow and profit.

    The 1 percent rule states that the gross monthly rental revenue should be at least 1% of the property purchase price after renovations. It is very unusual to hear about individuals using the 2 percent or even 3 percent Rule — the larger the percentage, the better.

    The 70 percent rule is a lesser-known guideline. This is a guideline for profitably acquiring and flipping distressed real estate, which specifies that the acquisition price should be less than 70% of the after-repair value (ARV) minus repair expenditures (rehab).

    Rate of return on investment

    Internal rate of return (IRR), also known as annualized total return, is the yearly rate received on each dollar invested for a year. Most utilize it widely, if not all investors, to compare various assets. The greater the IRR, the more appealing the investment.

    IRR is one of the essential measures of a rental property’s profitability; the capitalization rate is too simple, and Cash Flow Return on Investment (CFROI) does not account for the time value of money.

    A rental ROI of less than 4% is often not worth the investment (unless there are elements other than the statistics that make it worthwhile to consider). But an ROI of more than 10% is considered a good bargain by many.

    Using realistic and cautious values in your computation can provide a more accurate picture of your ROI.

    Be careful that lower-end properties, which typically seem to be more attractive on paper than mid-range and higher-end properties, might have greater tenant turnover and maintenance expenditures.

    The trick here is to predict greater vacancy and repair expenses to have a more realistic view of your expected ROI and not be disappointed when your original calculations don’t play out.

    Once you get your UAE Residence Visa, you also obtain your Emirates ID. Since you have to keep this document updated, it is important to know how to check the emirates id status.

    In this article, you are going to learn more about the emirates id status. Furthermore, you are going to understand how to replace it, apply for it, and much more. Let us observe:

    1. What is the Emirates ID?

    The Emirates ID Card is a document that the UAE issues to all individuals that apply for a UAE Residence Visa. Therefore, all UAE Residents must carry an Emirates ID with them. Your Emirates ID is issued after you get your residence visa. Thus, both documents have the same validity.

    In simpler words, it is the official identification card of the United Arab Emirates. So, if you want to comply with the law, you need to have this document with you. Moreover, you have to keep your emirates id status in order.

    Your Emirates ID consists of 15 digits. It is a unique number, thus two persons cannot have the same number. It contains critical information, and it is important to understand it:

    • 1st section: it is the UAE international code (784) and it is the same in all Emirates ID Cards.
    • 2nd section: it usually is your birth year. But, this is not always the case on all cards.
    • 3rd section: it is a randomly generated number
    • 4th section: it is a single digit from 0 to 9, which is a verification number

    Thus, your Emirates ID is personal and will remain the same even if you cancel your UAE Visa. You cannot modify or amend your number.

    2. Why is your Emirates ID status important?

    Your Emirates ID card is an essential document in the UAE. For this reason, you should know how to check your emirates id status to keep it updated.

    It is a crucial piece of identification in the Emirates, and thus you can use it for a variety of purposes. Whether you are residing in Abu Dhabi, Dubai, or any of the free zone regions of Sharjah, Umm al Quwain, Fujairah, Ajman and Ras Al Khaimah, you will need to use your Emirates ID for several processes, such as follows:

    • Rent an apartment or a house where you can live
    • Register a vehicle
    • When applying for government services like DEWA, or others
    • If you plan to sponsor your dependents with a family visa
    • Open a bank account
    • Pay internet and utility bills

    In addition, you will need to use your Emirates ID when you travel, since you will have to present it at the immigration gates.

    So, if you live in the UAE, whether you are a UAE Citizen, GCC national or expatriate, you need to have your Emirates ID.

    3. How can you check the validity of your Emirates ID?

    As we have mentioned before, you have to keep your Emirates ID updated. However, if you would like to check the validity of your Card first, you can do it in a few simple steps.

    The validity of an Emirates ID Card refers to the expiry date of your document. Thus, it is important to know when it expires so you do not have to face a fine or a penalty.

    You just have to do the following:

    • Go to the ICA Smart Services Portal
    • Select File Validity
    • Enter your Emirate Unified Number, nationality and date of birth
    • Click on search

    After that, you will see all the details about your Emirates ID card, such as its validity.

    4. How can you check your Emirates ID status?

    To check your emirates id status you just have to follow 3 quick and easy steps. The best part is that you can check it using your laptop or smartphone. However, you need to have your Emirates ID tracking number or registration application number.

    Next, you will have to do the following:

    1. If you are in the UAE, you can visit the Federal Authority of Identity and Citizenship website.
    2. Look for the section “Check ID Status” located on the right side
    3. Type your Emirates ID number or Application number without the hyphen
    4. Click on the arrow
    5. A window will appear with all the information about your Emirates ID

    You will see your application number, type, Emirates ID number, current status and next step. And, lastly, you will see your Application History Log.

    If you do not want to check it online, you can always call the authority.

    5. What is the process to renew the Emirates ID?

    Once you have checked the validity of your Emirates ID, you have to be aware of the expiry date to renew it when it is the right time. If you want to remain in the UAE, you need to renew your Emirates ID.

    However, rest assured, that the government grants a 30-day grace period for Emirates ID renewal. And, during this period you will receive an SMS with a reminder. If you fail to renew it, after the grace period is over you will have to pay a late renewal fine of AED 20 for each day.

    Therefore, to avoid this kind of situation, you have to renew it on time. Here’s what you need to do:

    1. Complete the Emirates ID Renewal Application form
    2. Pay the required fees
    3. Submit your form to a registered authority at the free zone or the GDRFA if it was issued on Mainland.

    Once you carry out the renewal process, you will get your new Emirates ID Card.

    6. What is the process to apply for an Emirates ID?

    The process to apply for an Emirates ID is pretty straightforward. You have to do it when you are carrying out your application for a UAE Visa. Once you have received your residence visa stamp, you have to go to an accredited typing centre to obtain this document.

    However, you can also obtain it through the ICP official website, by applying online. You have to choose the method that is simpler for you.

    It is important to have the required documentation to apply. You will need to provide your birth certificate and passport. Moreover, if you apply in person, you will undergo fingerprint scans and eye scans. This is to store your biometric data in the Authority’s system.

    And, once you want to renew it, you will not have to go through the scans once again.

    In case you have a freelance visa or are the owner of a business, you can apply for your Emirates ID by yourself. And, if you are under an employment visa, your employer has to apply for it on your behalf.

    But, if you find it very difficult to do it, you can always get support from experts. Here at Connect Middle East, we want to help you solve any issues you may have with immigration processes. Learn more about us and how we can help you.

    7. How much does it cost to get an Emirates ID?

    To calculate the cost of your Emirates ID you need to consider the expenses involved with the UAE Residence Visa. This is because the Emirates ID Card is included in the costs of your UAE Visa.

    The total cost may vary depending on which Emirate you carry out the process. However, the price of the Emirates ID ranges from AED 2,500 to AED 7,000.

    This is because the process for applying for a UAE Residence Visa includes the following costs:

    • Entry permit: you have to pay a fee for your entry permit. This helps you enter the UAE and it is valid for 60 days. During that period you can carry out the processes to obtain your visa and Emirates ID.
    • Medical check: it is mandatory to undergo a medical examination when you are applying for a UAE visa and Emirates ID.
    • Emirates ID Application: The total price includes the application for the Emirates ID.
    • UAE Visa stamping: you will get your visa stamped on your passport.

    In relation to the Emirates ID Cost, the price varies depending on its validity:

    • 1-year validity: AED 170
    • 2-year validity: AED 270
    • 3-year validity: AED 370

    After you make the payments and once you get your visa stamp, you should receive your Emirates ID Card within 7-10.

    8. How can you cancel your Emirates ID?

    In some circumstances you have to cancel your Emirates ID:

    • If you are leaving the UAE permanently.
    • If you are going to change your job, you are setting up a business in Dubai, or you are applying for a new UAE Visa.

    In this regard, you have to cancel your Emirates ID by following simple steps. You just have to submit your ID card to the immigration authority when you are submitting your visa cancellation.

    9. What is the process to replace a lost Emirates ID?

    It is important to take care of your documents to not lose them. You must keep them in a place where you can find them easily. However, in case you lost it, you have to get a new one immediately.

    In addition, you have to carry out additional steps:

    1. Go to a police station. You have to file a report for your missing Emirates ID Card. Keep in mind that you will have to pay a fee of AED 70.
    2. Contact the FAIC to report your Emirates ID Card is lost. Make sure to do this within 7 days of losing it.
    3. Go to any FAIC office to apply for a new card. You will have to pay AED 300 for the card and AED 70 for the application fee. In case you are requesting a new one online, the cost will be AED 300 plus AED 40 for the application fee.
    4. Get your new Emirates ID Card at an Emirates Post Office.

Plus, since you have gone through the process at least once, everything can flow properly.

    In this article, we will show you the steps to renew your visa, as well as the cost you must pay. Likewise, we will give you some tips so that you can successfully complete the procedure in any of the Emirates that make up the country.

    Understanding the Importance of Visa Renewal

    Through visa renewal UAE, as a freelancer, you can continue enjoying the benefits that the Emirates offers. Although the freelance visa has a validity period of 3 years, you must renew it annually. Therefore, if your freelance visa expires and you do not renew it, you will need to leave the country and make a new application.

    Since you have experienced what it means to work in the UAE on a freelance visa, you know the advantages of it.     Freelance Visa Renewal Process Dubai

    Visa renewal UAE is a process similar to requesting the document for the first time. This means that you must have all the necessary documents to be able to carry out the process smoothly.     Documents required for visa renewal UAE

    Depending on the business sector in which you carry out your independent activities, you will need to submit certain documentation. However, there are some common documents that you must have ready for Dubai visa renewal. The complete list includes the following documents:

    • Copy of your passport (you must have a copy of the passports of your dependents available if you are sponsoring a family member).
    • Photograph the same size as your passport.
    • Proof of educational and professional qualifications.
    • NOC (No Objection Certificate) from your employer if you work in a company.
    • Valid medical insurance.

    Freelance visa renewal process

    As a freelancer, you must be aware of the moment in which you must renew your visa according to the requirements of the authorities. We already mentioned that although the visa is valid for 3 years, you must renew your permit annually to continue your self-employment. Therefore, it is ideal to anticipate the expiration date and do the visa renewal UAE on time to avoid incurring legal problems.

    The renewal process includes the following steps:

    1. Gather all the documents we listed in the previous section.
    2. You will need to undergo a routine medical checkup to obtain a certificate of physical fitness necessary for renewal. Thus, before starting the process, make an appointment at an authorized healthcare facility in the UAE.
    3. Check the validity of your health insurance, if it has expired, you will need to get one that covers your self-employment.
    4. The next step is to renew your establishment card, which has an additional cost to the visa.
    5. Make the formal renewal request through the AXS platform. In this case, it is the TECOM business services platform.
    6. Then you will need to pay the visa renewal fee (which we will talk about later).
    7. Finally, if you have followed the process properly, you will receive your approval in 2 to 3 weeks.

    Once you get your renewed freelance visa, you will need to check all the details to ensure that all the information is correct. Otherwise, you must contact AXS to correct any erroneous information.

    Freelance visa cost

    Obtaining and renewing the self-employed visa in the UAE involves different costs, which we will break down below:

    • Permit cost. The visa renewal UAE (like the application) costs AED 7,500.
    • Establishment card. As with the visa, you must renew this card annually, for AED 2,000.
    • Work visa. The cost of this document depends on the validity period. Thus, the 3-year one costs AED 2,750, and the 5-year one costs AED 5,000.
    • Residence visa. In this case, the 3-year visa costs AED 3,330 (regular) or AED 3,900 (express) from outside the UAE. On the other hand, AED 4,960 (regular) or AED 6,340 (express) from the UAE.

    Additionally, you must consider the cost of health insurance, which varies depending on the coverage and the agency from which you purchase it. However, the visa cost includes stamping, medical tests, as well as the Emirates ID.

    2. Contact the visa issuing authority in the Ajman Free Zone.
    3. Then, pay any applicable renewal fees.
    4. Finally, you will receive your renewed freelance visa, with a validity period of 1 year from the date of issue.

    However, if you do not want to renew your visa, you can choose to cancel the document correctly. If you do not carry out this process according to legal regulations, you may face fines or legal action.

    Sharjah’s Approach to Freelance Visa Renewal

    In Sharjah, there are also specific rules for issuing freelance visas for foreigners. Nevertheless, there are no significant differences from the standards established in other Emirates. Therefore, renovation is a similar process, so you must consider the aforementioned aspects.

Therefore, with the facilities offered by the authorities, they encourage the work of freelancers who contribute to the local economy. For you, it represents the opportunity to continue growing professionally and take advantage of great opportunities.

    Common Mistakes to Avoid During the Renewal Process

    Although visa renewal UAE is a simple process to execute, there are aspects that you should not neglect. Therefore, we offer you in detail a list of mistakes that you should avoid so as not to interrupt or prevent your renewal.

    Expired passport

    • A common error not only in the application and renewal of freelance visas or other visas is the validity of the passport. This is one of the first requirements that the authorities review, since for renewal, you must have a valid passport and provide a copy. Therefore, you must verify that your passport has the necessary validity, or else your application will be denied.
    • Renew your passport if you want to continue working as a freelancer in the UAE, for which you will need to check with the authorities.

    Incorrect documents

    • We have already mentioned the common documents for visa renewal Dubai, Ajman, and Sharjah, so you should have them at hand.
    • Apart from the application form, you must submit these documents in full or your renewal application will be rejected.
    • For example, the photograph must be of the appropriate size, since the authorities are strict with each document.
    • If you work in a company while freelancing in your free time, you must submit the NOC. In this way, the authorities have the assurance that your employer has no problem with you carrying out activities outside of your regular employment.
    • Another supporting document is the medical examination, which must be certified in a health center authorized for this purpose.

    Therefore, make sure you have each document as required by the authorities at the time of visa renewal UAE.

    Form with errors

    • When requesting or renewing such an important document, it is extremely important not to make any mistakes, since the smallest one can mean a delay.
    • Review every aspect of the form and fill it out carefully, verifying at the end that each information is consistent with your data.
    • Above all, pay attention to where you must enter numerical data, which are the most common in which there are errors.

    Health insurance

    • Having health insurance is essential for foreigners visiting, residing, or working in the UAE.
    • This document must have the necessary coverage for the various activities you carry out in the country.
    • Not having adequate or valid medical insurance will hinder visa renewal.

    Expert Tips for a Successful Freelance Visa Renewal

    Renewing your freelance visa in the United Arab Emirates involves a series of processes that you must complete correctly. Thus, any mistake or missing any important step may result in a rejection of your application. Therefore, we offer you some important points for the process to be successful:

    • The NOC is an essential document for both the application and renewal of the visa. Therefore, agree with your employer to guarantee its delivery, since a company does not need to deliver it to a worker.

    Conclusion: Secure Your Freelance Future in the UAE

    Working as a freelancer in the UAE opens up a huge world of possibilities thanks to business opportunities. Guide for ICA Smart Services: Status, Approval & Entry

    In the UAE there are many governing bodies in charge of controlling documentation and immigration. Therefore, residents and expats should be aware of how to take advantage of the tools offered by them, and one of these is the smart services ICA.

    In this article, you are going to learn more about ICA smart services. Moreover, you are going to understand all the benefits of this tool. Let’s observe:

    1. What are ICA Smart Services?

    The Federal Authority for Identity and Citizenship, also known as ICA, is in charge of regulating the issuance of visas, and many other processes.

    In this regard, they have developed a system intending to support citizens, residents, and tourists. This is the ICA smart services. Its purpose is to facilitate the entry and exit of people in the UAE. Moreover, an individual can carry out additional tasks such as vaccine registration, and checking visa status, among others.

    Thus, it is an integrated service that anyone visiting the UAE should use. With this centralized portal, each person can access to a wide range of services.

    Additionally, it is available 24/7. Therefore, people can use it whenever they want since it has Smart Channels and E-services. And, it also has a mobile application. But, in case you do not want to access it online, you can also use the services by attending one of the ICA offices.

    One of the advantages of using this system is that the individual can submit his or her information to process the visa faster and easily.

    Here are the 9 priority services you can use through the platform:

    • Issue a residence permit.
    • Renew a residence permit.
    • Issue a new ID Card.
    • Renew your ID card.
    • Issue the entry permit.
    • Issue a new passport.
    • Renew your passport.
    • Issue your Family Book.
    • Modify the Family Book.

    2. Benefits of ICA Smart Service in UAE

    Since the ICA implemented this service, many people have used it to their advantage. Therefore, it offers comprehensive assistance to individuals, travelers, and business owners concerning immigration processes.

    Here we have the benefits of the ICA smart service UAE for individuals:

    • You can check your application online.
    • It is possible to use the services through any device: mobile, laptop, tablet, etc.
    • It admits application modifications online.
    • Make an appointment for residence entry in case it gets cancelled.
    • Check your visa status easily.
    • You can check if you have any visa fine.
    • It is possible to register your vaccines upon arrival.
    • You can update your Emirates ID.
    • It has many services available for tourists.

    3. Who are Eligible for ICA Smart Services?

    Anyone that wishes to travel to the UAE can use the ICA smart services. Whether you are an entrepreneur looking to start your business in Abu Dhabi, or a solid investor expanding their company to Dubai, you can benefit from this system.

    All you have to do is register on the website. Thus, registration is open to the following:

    • UAE Citizens: Emiratis can register and use services related to them, such as family book services, passport services, Emirates ID services, and others for the sponsored.
    • UAE Residents: through this system they can use services related to visa, residency, and Emirates ID. Both for them and their sponsor.
    • Visitors: individuals that want to visit the UAE can use the system for services related to entry visas.
    • GCC Citizens: they can use services related to the Emirates ID as well as to their sponsor.
    • GCC Residents: they can use services related to entry visas.

    As you can see, anyone is eligible for using the ICA services. Employees, business owners, freelancers, and representatives in Dubai can take advantage of all the services offered on this platform.

    4. How much you have to pay for ICA Smart Services?

    To register for the ICA smart services you have to pay a fee for registration. It is a single payment of AED 150 that you have to pay once you have arrived in Abu Dhabi or Dubai. Moreover, you can make the payment online, or at the ICA office.

    In case you want to track the progress of your application, once you have paid, you can use several means to do it:

    • Online account: with your ICA registration number that was sent by email, you can track your application.
    • Contact the ICA call centre: you can call an ICA operator at any moment to ask about your application. They work 24 hours a day.
    • Use the mobile App: log into the mobile app and check the status of your application.

    5. How to Access it?

    To access the ICA smart services you have to register first. Once you arrive at the airport, you have to go to the Smart Services counter and provide your Smart Number and nationality.

    Keep in mind that you must have your documentation with you. If you are planning to enter the UAE, you can carry out the register on arrival easily:

    1. Download the ICA UAE Smart App.
    2. Select “Register Arrival”.
    3. Fill in the data requested: application information, passport, addresses, vaccination, attachments, etc.
    4. You will be registered and now can use the system.

    However, you can carry out your registration before you arrive in the UAE. You can use the ICA Website and fill out the application. Submit it along with your Passport number, visa entry permit, and personal information.

    Once you have registered, you can access the system easily. You will receive an email with your ICA registration number. Thus, you can use it to track your applications or to use any other service available on the platform.

    5.1 How to use ICA Services?

    To use the system, you just have to visit the ICA Smart Services E-channel. Once you have entered the website, you can select the service you want to carry out.

    Go to the Smart Services Section, and select one of the categories: Citizens, UAE Residents, GCC Citizens, or Visitors. Alternatively, you can use the mobile application.

    So, to access the system, you will have to provide your information. It is a very simple process, and intuitive, so it is not difficult to use it.

    5.2 How to check ICA Smart Services Visa Status

    In case your visa has been issued by Sharjah, Abu Dhabi, Ajman, Fujairah, Umm al Quwain or Ras Al Khaimah, you can use the system to check your visa status and validity.

    Follow these simple steps:

    • Access the ICA Portal.
    • Click on “passport information”.
    • Select the visa type: “visa” or “residency”.
    • Provide your passport number and passport expiry date.
    • Select your nationality.
    • Click on search.

    If everything provided is correct, you will see all of your visa details.
