    For a foreigner, having a business setup in Dubai is a lucrative and exciting opportunity that has attracted entrepreneurs from all over the world. Dubai is an emirate whose main characteristics are its strategic location and its 0% tax rate. Another important and attractive point for foreigners is its simple incorporation procedure. Currently, the government has introduced several measures to further encourage foreign investment. For example, allowing expats to own 100% of their businesses in most cases.

    In this article, we will provide you with a complete guide on how to start a business as a foreigner in 2023. The intention is to cover all relevant aspects. That is, from the basic concepts of company formation to company structures for expatriates. In addition, we will give you a step-by-step guide on how you can create a company in this wonderful emirate.

    Business Ownership Rules for Foreigners

    If you want to setup a business in Dubai mainland and other freezones as a foreigner, you should know about business ownership. In this way, foreign investors have full ownership of specific companies. In addition, the participation of foreign investors will no longer be limited to a maximum of 49% as before but may reach 100%.

    This is based on the provisions of Federal Decree Law Number 26 of 2020. Where this law nullifies the requirement that commercial companies must have a major Emirati shareholder or agent. In this way, full foreign ownership is provided to non-Emiratis of all nationalities.

    In addition, companies can become joint stock companies, after approval from all relevant authorities; They can even sell no more than 70% of the company through initial public offerings. All this instead of the previous limit of 30%.

    Benefits for Foreign Entrepreneurs

    Currently, the United Arab Emirates (UAE) has some prosperous cities. For instance, Abu Dhabi and Dubai. These cities have become the best centers for doing business, which attracts investors and entrepreneurs from all over the world. If you are a foreign entrepreneur who wants to expand your horizons to form a company in the country, you can obtain many advantages.

    Below, you will see a list of all the benefits you can access to start a business in Dubai as a foreigner.

    Access to a strategic location and global markets: The UAE has a strategic location at the crossroads of Asia, Africa, and Europe. As a result, the country becomes an ideal launching pad for international businesses. Additionally, it offers easy access to markets beyond the Middle East.

    Business-friendly environment: This country has taken the task of fostering a business-friendly environment using various incentives. For example, the creation of numerous free zones, which offer 100% foreign ownership and tax exemptions. Furthermore, the best free zones in Dubai cater to various sectors. Among them, are technology, finance, logistics, and manufacturing.

    Economic stability: The United Arab Emirates has a diversified and stable economy, thanks to prudent fiscal policies and strong governance. One of the most significant advantages for foreign investors is that the risks involved in starting a business setup in Dubai as a foreigner are reduced.

    Tax benefits: One of the main attractions for starting a business in Dubai as a foreigner is the favorable tax regime of the UAE. Currently, there are no corporate or income taxes in most of the country, businesses in free zones can enjoy tax exemptions. As a result, you can generate substantial savings and greater profitability.

    Types of Business Licenses for Foreigners

    To start a business in Dubai as a foreigner is to choose one of the ideal types of trade licenses. Before starting the process of forming a company, you have to know all these types to be able to make the right choice. In essence, business activities are mainly classified into four business licenses. Below, you will see a detailed explanation of each of these.

    Commercial license: Commercial licenses in Dubai are issued to companies involved in the sale and purchase of products. The advantage of this license is that it allows you to start a business in Dubai as a foreigner who is dedicated to carrying out commercial activities.

    In Dubai, there are different types of business licenses available, for companies that are in the process of formation. To choose the correct one it has to be according to the specific commercial activity.

    Professional license: People who have academic achievements, competent skills, and intellectual abilities can access this license in Dubai. For instance, professionals, artisans IT service providers, and more. All of these can apply for a professional license.

    Industrial License: An industrial license in Dubai is necessary for companies that are involved in manufacturing materials and products in industries. These companies must have a physical office before issuing an industrial license.

    Freelancer Permit: If you want to be self-employed, you have to apply for the most popular business license in Dubai. That is the self-employed permit. It is important to mention that free zones offer this type of permit for individuals.

    Tourism license: This license is issued to companies that are dedicated to providing travel and tourism services. As Dubai is one of the most attractive tourist places in the world, this license is one of the most common among entrepreneurs.

    Step-by-Step Startup Process for Foreigners

    Now if you want to start a business in Dubai as a foreigner, this is the moment when you will see all the steps you have to follow. This is a process that consists of five simple steps and below you will see a good description of each of them.

    First step (hire experts): Although the process of starting a business in Dubai as a foreigner is simple, it is good to have the support of experts. Especially for you who are a foreigner since you do not know how the legal regulations are handled in the country. To find this expert company, it is advisable to look for reviews and comments from previous clients.

    Second step (choose your commercial activities): This is the most important step since the type of commercial activities will define other essential aspects. These aspects are the best configuration and type of commercial license for your business. For instance, if your business activities fall into the manufacturing or industrial group, the best license is the industrial one.

    Third step (choose between free zone and mainland): After doing complete research, you have to decide on the best location for your business. That is a free zone or continental zone. The truth is that there is no simple answer to this question because of all the aspects to take into account. For instance, the type of business.

    Fourth step (choose the name of the company): For the process of naming a company, you have to research all the existing regulations for registering the trade name.

    Fifth step (apply for business license): Finally, you have to apply for the business license. The process and the entity in charge will vary depending on whether you are in a free zone or a continental zone.

    Required Documents for Foreign Entrepreneurs

    The UAE government offers many incentives to foreign business owners to register their companies in Dubai. For this reason, documents are an important factor for you to register your company. Additionally, you must understand many free zones in the UAE and these are governed differently from mainland companies. Thanks to this, the necessary documentation will also change.

    Below, the necessary documents will be presented so that you can register your company in Dubai as a foreigner:

    • Submit the completed application form.
    • Your company’s business plan.
    • A copy of the Dubai registration certificate or business license.
    • A color copy of all the passports of the shareholders that the company will have and of the managers designated for it.
    • The signature model of the shareholders and managers designated for the new company.
    • An NOC from the current sponsor for individual businesses.

    Key Considerations for Expats Before Starting a Business

    Certainly, before starting a business in Dubai as a foreigner, there are certain considerations that you have to know. Below you will see a list of all these relevant and essential considerations for expats.

    Business culture in the UAE: Before starting a business in Dubai as a foreigner you have to understand the local business culture. While it is true, this nation is an attractive place to do business. In addition, the local government encourages investment and startups. Additionally, the government offers long-term visas for investors. As a result, there is currently a business boom in the country.

    Business visas in the UAE: If you want to start a business in Dubai as a foreigner, you will have to obtain a business visa. Currently, there are different types of visas available depending on your circumstances and needs.

    Business banking in the UAE: Once you begin business activities in the UAE, it is important to consider your banking options. In the country, there is a wide range of banking services for companies. For instance, the international Banks in Dubai.

    Hiring staff: If as a foreigner you plan to hire staff for your business in the UAE, it is important to comply with certain regulations. That is local labor laws. Additionally, you have to understand the regulations that are specifically with hiring and employment.

    Understand the legal structures for companies in the country: Currently, there are several legal structures for companies in the UAE. For instance, individual property, civil company, limited liability company (LLC), and others. The idea is to choose the one that best suits your business activities and needs.

    Cost Breakdown for Expat Entrepreneurs

    Business in Dubai for foreigners is a very important investment. Where the initial installation cost can reach 34,340 dirhams or 9,350 dollars. In addition, these amounts include various fees such as a general business license and charges for the Dubai Municipality, the Dubai Chamber of Commerce, and the Ministry of Economy.

    You also find additional costs such as rent and prerequisites for free zone business licenses. All of this influences the price and many companies may need up to $25,000 to set up the business.

    Business License Costs in Dubai: An industrial or service business license can cost between AED 10,000 and AED 50,000 per year.

    Employee and labor costs: The monthly salary range of an employee is between AED 4,810 to AED 99,000 per month.

    Operating costs and infrastructure: These costs in Dubai can change a lot. If you want to run a small business with an office size of 200 square feet you will need to know the following:

    • Office rental costs between 14,400 and 36,612 dollars.
    • Labor costs range between 160,138 and 214,744 dollars
    • On employee benefits you can spend between $49,900 and $65,600.
    • Internet and telephone would be 20,760 dollars
    • Electricity and water 324 dollars.

    Despite the costs, in the UAE the government has made launching businesses in Dubai easy. Furthermore, it is affordable through the implementation of new laws and policies. For this reason, pro-business tax policy is a very important selling point. Because, businesses do not have to pay local, state, or federal income taxes.

    Company Structure Options for Foreigners

    If you want to start a business in Dubai as a foreigner in the UAE, you have to first consider the type of structure you will form. Many different legal corporate structures exist in this nation. Below are some of the most common ones so you can make the best decision.

    Sole Proprietorship: This type of company has the main characteristic that it is 100% owned by a single person. That is, that person has full control over profits and operations. While it is true, all nationalities can create a sole proprietorship. However, only citizens of the UAE and the GCC can have an industrial or commercial company.

    Civil Company: All professionals with specific careers can open a civil company in the UAE. For instance, accountants, doctors, and lawyers. Of course, for this, an Emirati citizen must own 51% of the company’s shares.

    Limited Liability Company (LLC): In an LLC, there can be a minimum of two and 50 shareholders. The condition is that each one is responsible only for his percentage of shares. In addition, you have to know that profits and losses are divided among shareholders according to their shares.

    Foreign Company Branch: Foreign companies can establish a branch in this nation. In this case, the branches will be 100% owned by the parent company. However, the goods have to be imported through a local trading company.

    Freelancers: Believe it or not, setting up a freelance business is extremely easy in the UAE. The first thing will be to register in a free zone with an application form. In addition, you have to submit a bank reference, your CV, and a notarized Registry Identification Code form. Another advantage is that you can apply for a freelance visa.

    Conclusion: Expert Guidance for Foreign Entrepreneurs

    Starting a business in Dubai as a foreigner can be a rewarding and profitable opportunity. Additionally, thanks to its strategic location, a 0% tax rate, and a simple incorporation process; They make it one of the best destinations for businessmen from around the world.

    Introduction to Saudi Arabia’s Taxation Landscape

    Saudi Arabia has an exclusive tax system. As a result, it is one of the most remarkable features that determine the stability of the country’s economy.

    • The government of the country mainly has its revenue from oil. In addition, the leading sector can provide low tax rates for the people of this country. This does not apply to Saudi individuals’ income tax. Therefore, it becomes a voice for expatriates who are seeking for tax-free income.
    • Thus, in addition to the sales value tax (VAT) at the standard 5% rate on the supply of goods and services, the Saudi Arabia also introduces another tax on companies. The amount of those taxes depends on the company size. This tax was introduced has a part of the government’s efforts to aid the drivenness of its economy from the oil.

    In fact, VAT has been bringing on a lot of money to state. Also, has been accepted by commercial entities facilitating business setup in KSA.

    • Nonetheless, some particular industries in Saudi Arabia, like the sector of Islamic finance, are subject to specific taxes like Zakat. Without these industry-specific taxes, the market regulation and respecting Islamic principles would be hard to impossible.

    In addition, the government provides many incentives and tax exemptions for investor. This helps to boost the investment and drive economic expansion.

    • Consequently, Saudi Arabia does not follow the traditional income tax system but its taxation regime is rich. Therefore, this complex landscape means that the residents and business owners must be knowledgeable on the current tax regulations. This will help to elude any penalties or legal issues.

    In sip of that, it is possible to overcome the complexity of the tax in Saudi Arabia. Through effective channeling and advice for the beneficiaries you will perfectly understand the landscape of this taxation system.

    Overview of Saudi Arabia’s Taxation

    The tax in Saudi Arabia combines the locally customary property tax with the modern-day value added tax. The income tax is not as intricate as others, this has components for different sources of income. Here you have a deeper dive:

    • Corporate Income Tax. Business setup in Saudi Arabia is exposed to a corporate tax income of 20% on their total profits. Yet, there is a certain divisive part talking about. Profits acquired from the production of oil and gas have taxes that are 2-4 times the usual ones. Which ranges are normally from 50% to 85%.
    • Withholding Tax in Saudi Arabia. Foreign entities offering something in KSA without a permanent establishment are subject to a withholding tax in Saudi Arabia. Service charge is by the service recipients and the rate of deduction varies as follows: 5% – 20%. This is depending on the type of service given.
    • VAT Registration Threshold. The businesses with a total annual supply value exceeding SAR 375,000 (around $100,000 USD) must register for VAT. Hence, small businesses mainly reject VAT administration here since it is a complex and time-consuming task.
    • Zakat Exemptions. Besides, Zakat must be only on the assets which are not exempted for Muslims according to Islam. There are some exemptions in the bankruptcy laws. For instance, the basic household furnishings and the primary residence are included. The same is true for the personal belongings of a debtor.

    In addition, the Saudi government has put in place tax exemptions as part of the effort to attract foreign direct investment. These tax holidays on certain industries can play a major role in significantly reducing the tax burden of businesses who qualify for them.

    In sum, the tax in Saudi Arabia combines a benefit for citizens with an expatriate income tax and a consumption tax (VAT).

    Types of Taxes in Saudi Arabia

    The tax in Saudi Arabia consists of two types of taxes: indirect tax and direct tax. The direct taxes are for individuals or companies regarding to their income or profits. The indirect taxes are for goods and services at the selling point already realized.

    • Indirect taxes, and especially the one under Zakat, in Saudi Arabia are corporate income tax, individual income tax, and Zakat. Companies that run their businesses in the country have to pay corporate income tax based on their profit. At present the tax rate for corporate income tax remains unchanged at 20% for most business.

    However, they are few industries whose tax rate is 50%, such as the oil exploration and production business.

    • Meanwhile, the income tax for individuals is for Saudi citizens and residents. The rates of individual tax depend on the level of their income and ranges between 0% till 30%. People living above a certain financial capability and residents also needs to pay Zakat.
    • In addition to direct taxes, Saudi Arabia also imposes a value-added tax (VAT) on the sale of goods and services. Introduced in 2018, VAT currently stands at a rate of 15%. This tax applies to both domestic and imported goods and services.

    However, the country is not standing still and recently introduce a number of changes as a drive for diversity of income sources. The most important reform is the placing of excise taxes on harmful caloric drinks.

    • Excise taxes have exactly the same purpose: to discourage increasing consumption of the above-mentioned products. Also, assist the government with receiving additional revenue.

    Furthermore, one outstanding feature is the setting up of the General Authority for Zakat and Tax as the main authority. GAZT is an agency responsible for monitoring and collecting all taxes, deals with the tax laws and regulations enforcement.

    Value Added Tax (VAT)

    Tax on Value Added (VAT) has earned a great deal of respect globally as a good method of generating revenues for governments. Likewise, like other countries, the Kingdom of Saudi Arabia has included VAT in its fiscal reforms.

    • Therefore, the Saudi government started to apply the Value Added Tax (VAT) from January 1st, 2018 according to the GCC terms. This agreement was about broadening the funding basis of GCC states and alleviating their oil dependencies. Besides, it will enhance the fiscal sustainability and strengthen the economy of the country.

    Actually, the VAT has become more and more prominent source of non-oil revenue for Saudi Arabia. Before this implementation, the major source of revenue for the kingdom was oil, making it susceptible to fluctuations the oil prices. Through the introduction of VAT, the Saudi government is targeting to have a stable and sustainable economy.

    • As a first measure, Saudi Arabia introduces a locally known Value Added Tax (VAT) at a standard rate of 15%. VAT, as a levy imposed on most commodities and services sold within the country, is the most common tax in most nations. This markup is usually added to the products selling price that the customer will pay.
    • VAT-registered businesses get the privilege of collecting VAT from their customers, but must later contribute this money to the government. As a result, this can lead to an increase in the price hike for the customers.

    Without a doubt, VAT produces a major effect on business and consumer in Saudi Arabia. Businesses have to register for VAT if their annual revenue exceeds the GAZT set threshold of the Saudi Arabia General Authority of Zakat and Tax. This compliance requirement brings upon an equal ground for businesses operating and permit business setup in Saudi Arabia.

    Corporate Income Tax 

    Corporate tax of Saudi Arabia federal government is one of the main sources of revenue along with other sources. As a result, it becomes one of the key actions in funding public services and infrastructure development.

    • The corporate tax UAE structure consists of two main components: income tax and Zakat. Income tax is levied on foreign investors with a flat tax rate of 20% at the end of the fiscal year on net adjusted earnings. Furthermore, the withheld tax rates can vary from 5% to 20% depending on the type of income generated.
    • The system differs for Saudi Arabian and GCC citizen investors. They do not pay income tax but rather Zakat, an Islamic wealth tax. Zakat is charged at the rate of 2.5% on the company’s Zakat base, calculated as net assets on a Zakat basis. Therefore, tax burden for local investors is very low compared to those of foreign investors.

    However, there are some exceptions to this typical form. Exemption of tax is the privilege of oil and gas industries and mining. There is no incidence of corporate income tax, Zakat, or any other similar levy in these industries. Nevertheless, such industries can be exempted from certain types of tax regime or granted tax holidays.

    Certainly, this low tax rate has done more than anything else to attract investments and business setup in Saudi Arabia. It is clearly that the low tax rate has led to foreign investments and contribute to economic growth since then.

    Nevertheless, complying with the tax laws and regulations is a must for businesses working in Saudi Arabia. Absence of this measure may result in fines and legal repercussions. Thus, is advisable to refer a tax expert. This will help with more specialized knowledge of the industries which are the subjects of tax rules.

    Recent Changes and Updates in Saudi Arabia’s Tax System 

    Recently, Saudi Arabia’s tax system has come under the spotlight with some of the changes that it has undergone. Such amendments are mainly meant to promote transparency, ease processing routines and new financial burdens on businesses and taxpayers.

    • One outlined improvement relates to factual changes in the Income Tax Law. Consequently, these modifications include the holdback tax applied to payments paid to non-residents.

We invite you to join us and explore the following points in more detail:

    1. What is a UAE Tax Residency Certificate?

    Among the advantages of having a company in the UAE is that by registering a company in a free zone, the entrepreneur can obtain a UAE Tax Certificate. In simple words, a UAE Tax Residency Certificate is a document from the Ministry of Finance that certifies the residence of a natural or legal person.

    The tax residence certificate is meant for any resident company that carries out its commercial activities in the country, including free zone companies, such as businesses operating in the continental territory. This means that the company can take full advantage of the benefits resulting from the treaties to avoid double taxation.

    The main objective of this document is to confirm that the United Arab Emirates is the legal residence of the person or company; meaning that they will not have to pay taxes on the earnings generated in the nation. You should note that this advantage does not apply to offshore companies, also known as International Business Companies (IBC). Instead, these businesses may be eligible to receive a tax-exempt certificate.

    2. Why should you apply for this certificate?

    Knowing the definition of Tax Residence Certificate, these are the main advantages of having this document:

    • As mentioned above, an entrepreneur in the UAE can avoid double taxation between the UAE and their country. This will prevent them from paying taxes generated in their country of origin.
    • When setting up a business in the UAE, it is an essential requirement to have a tax residence certificate in order to access international markets.
    • In the case of the United States, its legislation establishes that citizens and those with permanent residence must pay taxes whether or not they reside in the country. If the same year you paid the taxes, you became a resident of the UAE, you can claim this payment.

    In general terms, the main advantage sought is to avoid double taxation, and to achieve this two conditions must be met:

    • That the foreign entrepreneur obtains the tax residence certificate in the UAE.
    • That the foreign entrepreneur is originally from a country with which the UAE has signed an agreement that avoids double taxation.

    3. How to apply for a UAE Tax Residency Certificate?

    First of all, remember that both natural and legal persons can obtain this certificate and that the TDC serves as official ratification before the competent body on the fiscal residence of a natural or legal person in the UAE.

    3.1 Requirements for natural persons

    • Copy of the applicant’s valid passport.

    • Bank movements of the last six months in the UAE.
    • Valid certification document in the UAE. For example, a contract, or salary certification.
    • Immigration report.
    • Copy of the lease agreement or home ownership title.

    3.2 Requirements for Companies

    Companies must also meet certain conditions and provide specific documents before opting to obtain a Tax Residence Certificate. To prevent an extended process and financial losses, they must always ensure that they meet all the requirements.

    • Copy of valid trade license.
    • Lease contract or property title of a commercial establishment of a minimum of three months before making the request.
    • Copy of the valid passport of the company’s legal representative.
    • Copy of the visa and Emirates ID of the company’s director/manager.
    • The latest audited financial statement containing the bank movements of the UAE company for the last six months; stamped by the bank.

    The documents will be submitted together with the application to the Ministry of Finance. If the application is approved, they will issue a Tax Residence Certificate in a period of approximately three weeks.

    4. Steps to apply for this document

    To make the request, you must visit the Federal Tax Administration website. Then, complete the registration form.

    4.1 Create a Tax Certificate account for new users

    First, you must register on the website and create a new account. Keep in mind that you will need to enter the following information:

    • Email address.
    • Name.
    • Username.
    • Address.
    • ZIP code.
    • Key code.
    • Password.
    • Security code.
    • Security response.
    • Answer suggestion.

    4.2 Access

    The user will be directed to the login page where the username and password will be requested. When logged in, the user can see the status of the request. Also, the user will be shown the following statuses for the submitted request:

    • Draft: This means the form has not been completed or submitted.
    • Draft awaiting payment: The user has reached the payment stage but it has not been made.
    • Pending: Submitted and awaiting approval. To be processed within 3 days.
    • Returned: This means that it is necessary to provide more information or documentation.
    • Pending payment: Here, the request was approved, and you must pay the corresponding fee to download the certificate.
    • Issued: The process was completed successfully and the certificate was issued.
    • Rejected: The request was rejected due to not fulfilling all the requirements.

    5. Eligibility criteria

    The eligibility criteria to obtain a UAE Tax Residency Certificate will also vary depending on whether the applicant is a natural or legal person.

    • Natural persons

    The applicant must be a resident of the UAE for at least the last 180 days. It is also important that you prove that you have a housing lease for a minimum of one year.

    • Legal persons

    To be eligible to obtain a TRC, the legal entity must be established for at least a one-year period. The financial statements must be certified by an accounting firm. This financial report must cover the fiscal year corresponding to the date of the request for the certificate. If the certificate is for the current year, the report must cover the previous year.

    6. How much does it cost to obtain a UAE Tax Residency Certificate?

    The cost is another factor that will vary according to whether the applicant is a natural or legal person. The cost for applying for the Tax Residency Certificate is higher in legal entities since they bring greater capital to the country and demand a greater number of requirements to process this document.

    More specifically, these are the costs to obtain the UAE Tax Residency Certificate:

    • Legal persons: From AED 568 to AED 1842. This is equivalent to 155 to 500 American dollars.
    • Natural persons: AED 1077.50. This is equivalent to 300 American dollars approximately.

    7. What is double taxation?

    Today, the business world is a global trading platform. International trade is at the fore, and the UAE is one of the world’s main business hubs today, helping improve commercial partnerships between countries. However, at the same time, entrepreneurs face certain problems when there is a tax conflict.

    This is when, due to the laws of their country of origin, they must pay taxes on the commercial activity they carry out abroad. In other words, the country where you carry out this commercial activity will require you to pay the corresponding taxes.

    Likewise, the tax residence certificate issued by the UAE authorities is beneficial for natural and legal persons. Anyone who obtains this certificate has the benefit of protection from the Double Taxation Treaty (DTT) that prevents this tax conflict between the signatory countries.

    Double taxation refers to imposing the same tax several times on a taxpayer who has the same income, based on a single generating event. Likewise, international double taxation is defined as a situation in which the same income or the same good is subject to taxation in two or more countries during the same taxable period and for the same reason.

    This is what a person prevents by obtaining this certificate as long as the UAE has signed a treaty to avoid double taxation with the country from whom this certificate is requested.

    UAE Visa cancellation process is an essential prerequisite. It is vital for keeping a good rapport with immigration office when you run out of the period of your authorized stay in UAE. Not canceling your visa on time can pose a different set of challenges. Such as the difficulties you may encounter when attempting to visit the same country in the future or even fines and legal issues.

    In this article, we will be discussing visa cancellation. A topic that we are going to cover from scratch until the end. We will discuss are the importance of your UAE visa cancellation process, the cases when is necessary and the overall process. Whether it is completing your stay, changing your visa type, or other situations.

    Understanding the Importance of Visa Cancellation

    A proper visa cancellation is an important stage in the process of maintaining the immigration authorities’ good standing. Preventing possible problems in the future. Here is why UAE visa cancellation process holds significant importance:

    • Avoids future issues: An un-cancelled, pending visa can lead to difficulties. For instance, when you re-attempt entry into the UAE the next time. Immigration officials may inquire about your reasons or even refuse an entry if you do not have properly resolved previous visa status.
    • Prevents fines and penalties: In most cases it will be necessary that the travelers pay a fine or a penalty if they fail to specify their departure from the territory by canceling their visa. The fee structure also depends on the time period you have overstayed and the particular circumstances in the UAE, but not by the total amount of money you owe.
    • Ensures future visa applications are smooth: An invalid visa may create an unfavorable impression on the future applications for a visa. It shows a disregard for the import operating processes and might result in allegations of being non-compliant to the government regulations.
    • Maintains a positive immigration history: Properly canceling your visa shows, you are a reliable person, and you fully understand and comply with immigration rules. Providing such valuable experience will give you an advantage in future visa applications. On the other hand, it may enhance your chances of approval.

    Following the cancellation of the visa process and understanding the consequences of overruling the visa will ensure a smooth departure. Also, you will avoid any unnecessary issues in the future.

    Significance of Visa Cancellation

    The implications of not canceling your visa can be very wide since it can affect your travel plans in the future. Here is a closer look at the potential repercussions of failing to take this crucial step:

    • Difficulties entering again: Your application can turn down if the immigration staff see you have an old canceled visa from the last visit. This might happen on regular border checks or on application for a new visa to travel to the same country.
    • Negative impact on other visa applications: Visa officials from different nations frequently exchange information. A previously canceled visa in one country may only be trouble when trying to obtain visas to any other country. Under these circumstances, applicants might experience more rigorous review, there could be delays or rejections in the application process.
    • Potential legal issues: If you overstay your visa or do not cancel it, it can be proof of your involvement in illegal immigration. As a result, causing legal consequences such as fines, imprisonment, and even banned from getting a new visa.
    • Financial implications: Apart from financial implications that may come along with an overstay, failure to cancel a visa can also increase the cost of the application.

    Be aware of the substantial consequences of not canceling your visa. By making such an assessment, you will be able to make the right decision on how to avoid illegal exit from the nation.

    When is Visa Cancellation Required?

    There are numerous cases that ask for you to cancel your visa, but there are some cases that you simply have to abide by. Here are some common scenarios that necessitate visa cancellation:

    • Completing your stay and leaving the country: This is the simplest scenario in which you need to cancel the visa after the duration authorized has expired and you leave the UAE.
    • Changing your visa type: If you wish to change your visa type while still in the UAE. For example, from a tourist visa to a UAE business visa, you might have to cancel your current visa and then apply for the new one.
    • Having your visa application rejected: If your visa application is rejected for a new visa, canceling your current visa might be demanded. Depending on the specific case and the regulations.
    • Death of visa holder: In case of a visa holder’s death, the sponsor or family must initiate the cancellation process.
    • Experiencing a change in employment or sponsorship: For employment visas, an alteration of your employment status. A situation such as job loss or changing your company, leads to your visa cancelation, most likely initiated by your old employer. Moreover, conditions for family or dependent visas might be canceled whenever sponsorship status makes adjustments.
    • Personal reasons: When you quit your job abruptly because of a medical emergency or some other unexpected situation. Consequently, requiring you to leave the country way before the planned time, may oblige the organization to cancel your visa.

    These are just some general cases and, actually, the UAE visa cancellation process might vary. It is always advisable that you check for the latest and most accurate information regarding the cause of your visa cancellation at the GDRFA official government site.

    Initiating the Visa Cancellation Process

    Finally asking how to cancel your visa and what next is the process of the cancellation. Here is a general overview of the initial steps:

    • Contact the relevant authorities: Figure out the right organization that has the power to hold the visa revocations. In the UAE these duties correspond to the GDRFA (General Directorate of Residency and Foreigners Affairs). You can get to the official website by searching for contact information.
    • Gather necessary documents: You need your passport and copies of it. The visa cancellation form (which is often available on the embassy/consulate website). Proof of your presence (e.g. boarding pass, sortie ticket), and the papers specifically required for a selected visa type (e.g. proof of work termination for work visas).
    • Schedule an appointment (if required): In certain cases, the authorities may need you to make an appointment before you go to submit your visa cancellation request. Check the website or directly communicate with the embassy/consulate, and their guidelines for applying for a visa.

    Before initiating the process, it is highly advisable to:

    • Review the official website of the GDRFA: This is perhaps the most accurate source of information about visa-cancellation policies. In addition to showing, you the required documents, fees, and processing times.
    • Consult with an immigration lawyer (optional): Visa cancellation remains a tasking issue for most immigrants. You can seek for legal advice. They can give you the necessary guides, assist you in all the processes, and handle situations if they arise.

    Employment Visa Cancellation

    Cancellation of a job visa usually requires joint efforts from both the employee and the employer. Next, we describe the process:

    • Initiation: UAE visa cancellation process normally starts with the employer who undertakes to alert the various authorities of your contract termination. This initiates with the termination of your work permit/status with the Ministry of Human Resources and Emiratisation (MOHRE). It means getting your signature on some specific documents and making sure that your employer clears all the outstanding bills for you.
    • Employee’s involvement: Employer will be responsible to notify the GDRFA to initiate the UAE visa cancellation process that will occur after the work permit is canceled. You might need to supply your original passport, Emirates ID, including a letter of your employment termination.
    • Exit procedures: Visa cancellation may involve completion of this procedure. Along with a disclaimer, that your visa has been canceled. These processes include clearing tax debts, visiting the competent agencies for the approval, or even undergoing a medical examination.

    Keep under consideration that visa cancellation procedures and the specific requirements that may apply in your case may be slightly different. Depending on the of employment and the terms and conditions of your employment contract to which you are bound for.

    It is crucial to consult with your employer, relevant parties. As well as the appropriate authorities beforehand in order to have an easy and lawful cancellation process.

    Family or Dependent Visa Cancellation

    For family or dependent visas, the cancellation process frequently involves the sponsor and the visa holder. Here is a glimpse into the potential steps:

    • Initiation: The holder of the visa itself or by the sponsor can start this process according to the specific circumstances. For some occasions, both parties have to be part.
    • Required documents: Besides simple papers like passport and visa, documents of the sponsorship and perhaps necessitate additional documents. Such kinds of evidence may be of a different nature. For instance, divorce decree, cancellation of sponsorship agreement, or certification proving that the person is not a dependent anymore.
    • Considerations for minors: Visa holders who are minors need any extra requirements or permission of an authorized person. Talking to an immigration lawyer will be of great value in encountering the process for minors. Since it is sometimes difficult for minors to go through this process themselves.

    In order to ensure the smoothness or success of the process, there is a need for consultation with the appropriate authorities. In addition, acquiring necessary professional advice when needed.

    Once you are familiar with the specific cancellation procedures for different types of visas, you have a great chance of knowing all the steps required. Therefore, not being surprised by any unforeseen complexities.

    Document Preparation and Submission

    Expediting the visa cancellation process in the UAE basically depends on whether documents are well prepared and presented. In this phase, we will examine the mandatory documents needed, review different submission options. Moreover, we will give tips on how to have straightforward and efficient practice.

    • Ensure all documents are complete and accurate: All details on the forms should be double-checked. And you should be in possession of all the documents officially as well as photocopied.
    • Translation requirements: In case if documents are not in the native language, then you may need language certified translation.
    • Organize the documents: Classify your documents clearly. Keeping as organized as you can a checklist to make sure you do not miss anything.

    Required Documents

    The exact documents which need to be presented or exempted from visa cancellation in the UAE depend on your visa type and your personal situation. However, it is pertinent to know the general requirements beforehand.

    • Original passport: This document proves your identity and travel authorization. We suggest you to have the expiry date at least 6 months beyond your planned departure date.
    • Original Emirates ID: This is an official card you need to present for your residency status among the UAE population. Make sure it has no defects or damage on it.
    • Visa cancellation application form: Submit this document to the immigration office of GDRFA. This document has to be filled in correctly and signed by the required parties.
    • Employment visa: After starting the cancellation process, the employer will usually enter this information in the form for you.
    • Family/dependent visa: The sponsor can be either a family member or a family friend. They will sign the form and be responsible for all its contents.

    Divers visa types have additional requirements which must be met, like:

    • Marriage certificate: Used for filling the forms of spousal visa termination.
    • Birth certificate: Essential with dependent visa, particularly for children.
    • Proof of exit ticket: A proof of your booking for your departure may be requested at times from the GDRFA. For instance, a confirmed reservation of a flight.
    • No liability certificate (optional): Though not always necessary, getting this certificate from your bank is a good sign that there are no outstanding debts in the UAE.
    • Translation of documents (optional): If any of your documents are not in Arabic, it may be required to have them translated by a certified translator. Also, you need to submit the original version as well as the translated one.

    Visa Cancellation Form Submission

    The process of form-filling of cancellation visa writing may differ based on policies and procedure. Here are some common ways:

    • In-person submission: One of the several avenues to apply DM penalty is by going to the GDRFA office. Presenting the required documents and paying the associated fees. This option essentially entails a face-to-face meeting with the authorities and also letting them clear off any shortcomings during the current procedure.
    • Online submission: You can pay your fees online via GDRFA portals provided by a few emirates as well. In the portals, you can upload scanned copy of your documents for your ease. Although it spares the effort of mailing and receiving papers, this method should additionally safeguard ensuring every document is clearly scanned and submitted accordingly.
    • Mail-in submission: In some extremely rare cases, some countries would also look at the mailed applications. Although, this method can be discouraged at times as it may lead to delays whereas the documents may get lost while in transit.

    In whichever presentation format you decide on, make sure to include all the necessary attachments together with the filled form. Incomplete and filled-out forms may result in long-term waiting or the process being conducted entirely in vain.

    Being a proactive applicant and mastering all the required documents and choosing the most effective submission method, you can gain your chances as high as possible and be granted with successful and efficient UAE visa cancellation process.

    Visa Cancellation Approval and Final Steps

    The successful conclusion of the UAE visa cancellation process involves securing the official approval. Which marks the final step of the procedure. This is the last stage where the following important steps will be highlighted in more detail.

    Processing Time:

    • The duration of the visa cancellation approval can widely differ, depending on your case complexity and also of the current workload of authorities. The process time could be 2-3 days to a few weeks or months in some scenarios.
    • Checking the status: You may do online checking of your application. Or even contacting the General Directorate of Residence and Foreigners Affairs.

    • These fees can include the cost of the cancellation, administration fees, and maybe the late penalty if there be one.

    Visa Cancellation Approval

    When you send your visa-cancellation application, you will have to wait and see until the authorities make their decision on canceling your visa. Processing times vary widely depending on the complexity of your case, and the volume of work they are currently having. It might end up being for a couple of days to several weeks or, in some cases, even months.

For this reason, and if you want to obtain your digital nomad visa in Dubai, you got to the right place.

    In this article, we will dwell on the world of digital nomads: what they are, the benefits and obligations of becoming one, the different types of visas you can apply to as a digital nomad (as well as the different visa services in the UAE), and a detailed guide on how to get a digital nomad visa in Dubai.

    Unveiling the Digital Nomad Visa in Dubai

    The digital nomad visa in Dubai is a special type of visa that allows individuals from other countries to reside in the city for a maximum of one year, while working remotely for their employers located outside of the UAE.

    Firstly, it allows approved individuals to obtain a residential ID; granting them access to public services and amenities just like any other resident of Dubai. This visa has a duration of one year, with the opportunity of renewal if they wish to do so. Besides, the application process typically takes around five to seven days, and it is a very smooth procedure. Additionally, family members can be included in the application.

    Moreover, since the digital nomad visa in Dubai was only recently stablished in 2020, the requirements are often changing. For instance, one of the recent modifications was the minimum income requirement. In 2022, the minimum income was set at 3,500 USD per month, but in 2023, it was raised to 5,000 USD.

    Furthermore, given the relatively recent introduction of this visa, it is possible that certain government offices may not be well-versed in its specifics. Consequently, major banks may decline requests to open bank accounts or apply for credit cards based on this visa type.

    It is also important to remember that this type of visa does not lead to permanent residency in the UAE. However, the visa can be easily renewed for additional one-year periods if so desired.

    Introduction to Digital Nomadism

    Digital nomadism refers to a lifestyle where people engage in remote work while constantly traveling and residing in different locations. It grants them the freedom to select their preferred work setting, such as cafes, shared workspaces, libraries, or even hotel rooms. The growth of digital economy and the availability of remote job options have played a significant role on digital nomadism.

    • Distinctively, digital nomads reside in a particular place for a brief period; lasting from a few weeks to several months, before proceeding to a different location. Alternatively, they may opt for a more frequent lifestyle of continuously switching cities or even countries.
    • Additionally, digital nomads use technology, such as laptops and smartphones, to carry out their work remotely from any location that has an internet connection. They depend on internet access and communication tools, like voice over IP, to stay connected with their clients and colleagues.
    • The digital nomad visa, specifically the Dubai Remote Working Visa, allows digital nomads to reside and work remotely in Dubai. This means that digital nomads employed by a company located outside of the UAE can apply for the digital nomad visa in Dubai.
    • Moreover, during their stay in Dubai under the digital nomad visa, individuals are classified as tax residents in the UAE. This implies that, as the UAE imposes a 0% income tax rate, digital nomads are exempt from paying income tax.
    • On top of that, Dubai imposes no limitations on eligibility for obtaining a trade license. Anyone with a valid Emirates ID can apply for a one-year trade license, enabling them to generate multiple streams of income; as long as they engage in activities within their respective areas of expertise and follow all established regulations.

    Understanding the Visa Concept

    The distinctions between the freelance visa in Abu Dhabi, freelance visa in Dubai, and the digital nomad visa in Dubai can be summarized, can be summarized as follows:

    • The freelance visa in Abu Dhabi can be obtained through the Abu Dhabi Department of Economic Development. It is a freelancer permit that allows individuals to work as freelancers within the media production and entertainment industries. The permit is valid for two years and requires meeting specific eligibility criteria.
    • On the other hand, the freelance visa in Dubai offers multiple avenues for freelancers to work with employers within Dubai; such as the GoFreelance program administered by the Dubai Development Authority. This program covers four sectors, which means freelancers can choose from a wider range of activities within these sectors. The freelance visa in Dubai has a validity of one year and you can easily renew it.
    • Finally, the digital nomad visa in Dubai grants individuals the opportunity to reside and work remotely in Dubai for up to one year.
    • The digital nomad visa provides a temporary residence permit to live in Dubai, and does not lead to permanent residency; in this, it significantly differs from the Silver visa and the Golden visa in the UAE as well. The latter allow you to stay in the UAE for up to 5 to 10 years respectively, after which you can apply for permanent residence.
    • Therefore, while both freelance and digital nomad visas cater to independent workers, the key difference lies in their scope. Freelance visas limit you to working with local businesses in the city; in contrast, the Dubai digital nomad visa exclusively caters to remote work with overseas employers.

    Applying for the Dubai Digital Nomad Visa

    Any individual employed by companies located outside the UAE are eligible to apply for a digital nomad visa in Dubai. The application process usually lasts approximately five to seven days, in which you must remain in the city.

    To apply, individuals simply need to collect the required documents, such as a valid passport, proof of income of at least 5,000 USD per month or 60,000 USD per year, and health insurance with UAE coverage. In addition, you can submit the application online via the official Work Remotely from Dubai website; the portal in charge of the digital nomad visa services in the UAE.

    The digital nomad visa in Dubai remains valid for one year, enabling successful applicants to obtain a residential ID. This grants them access to public services and amenities like any other Dubai resident. Additionally, if the applicant desires to continue their stay and work in the city, the visa can be easily renewed in annual-periods.

    Eligibility Criteria

    To be able to qualify for the digital nomad visa in Dubai, which is also referred to as the Dubai Remote Working Visa, you must meet certain criteria. Below are the essential eligibility requirements:

      • Minimum Income. You must have a monthly income of at least 5,000 USD.
      • Occupational Flexibility. The digital nomad visa is available for freelancers, entrepreneurs, and remote workers.
      • Valid Passport. You need to have a passport with validity for a minimum of six months.
      • Health Insurance. It is mandatory to have health insurance that provides coverage in the UAE.
      • Global Eligibility. The digital nomad visa is open to applicants from all over the world, without any specific age or language proficiency requirements.

    Application Process

    In order to submit an application for the digital nomad visa in Dubai, you need to adhere to the following sequence of steps:

    • First, you must fill out the application form. For this, you can visit the official Work Remotely from Dubai website and fill out the online visa application form.
    • Then, gather and send the required documents. These include a valid passport, proof of monthly income of at least 5,000 USD, and health insurance with UAE coverage validity.
    • In addition, you must pay the established fees. The general cost can vary depending on the individual requirements and the specific services required. Nonetheless, here is a breakdown of the approximate:
      1. Premium health insurance: 2,000 USD
      2. Entry permit: 1022,50 AED (278 USD)
      3. Status change: 672.50 AED (183 USD)
      4. Health checkup: 354 AED (96 USD)
      5. Temporary Residency Visa: 393.50 AED (107 USD)
      6. Emirates ID application: 341.7 AED (93 USD)
      7. Biometrics test: 254.55 AED (69 USD)
    • After you take care of the fee payment, it comes the application review. This means the relevant authorities will review each step of your application and documents.
    • If your application is successfully approved, you will receive an email extending a warm welcome to Dubai as a digital nomad. Upon approval, you will also be issued a residential ID, granting you access to all public services and facilities like other residents of Dubai.

    Navigating Legalities and Regulations

    Digital nomads must adhere to various regulations and laws as they navigate their remote work lifestyle. From visa requirements and immigration regulations to tax obligations and compliance with local labor laws, understanding and following these legalities is crucial for a seamless and lawful digital nomad experience. By staying informed and proactive, digital nomads can ensure a smooth, hassle-free journey while exploring the world.

    Legal Obligations

    If you choose to be a digital nomad in the UAE, it is important to understand and fulfill certain legal responsibilities. Here are a few essential considerations to keep in mind:

    • First, digital nomads in Dubai must acquire a UAE residency visa, specifically the Dubai Remote Working Visa; enabling them to reside and engage in remote work in Dubai for up to one year. The visa requires meeting certain requirements, which have been previously addressed.
    • Additionally, individuals who reside in Dubai under the digital nomad visa are tax residents in the UAE. This means that digital nomads in Dubai may benefit from the UAE’s zero percent income tax rate in certain jurisdictions; thus being exempt from income tax obligations.
    • Moreover, the UAE has implemented regulations to safeguard online data and privacy. The Federal Decree Law No. 34 of 2021 specifically addresses concerns regarding the misuse and exploitation of digital technologies. Its objective is to strengthen protection against online crimes carried out through the utilization of information technology, networks, and platforms.
    • It is crucial to understand the legal consequences of working remotely from another country if you are operating for a company outside the UAE. Employment laws vary across countries, and it is important to consider the requirements of each country to prevent any potential legal complications.
    • Lastly, for digital nomads, effective financial management is essential. To open a bank account in the UAE, certain documents such as identification documents, proof of residency (e.g., your visa), and proof of income are necessary.

    Visa Duration and Renewal

    Overall, the Dubai digital nomad visa remains valid for one year, and you can easily renew it if you wish to extend your stay in Dubai. This is generally a very smooth procedure, but depending on a variety of things the process can take longer. This is why the UAE visa grace period is really useful.

    The UAE visa grace period refers to the extra duration provided to individuals after the expiration of their visa; allowing them to either renew their visa or make necessary arrangements to depart from the country. The length of the grace period can vary depending on the type of visa and individual circumstances.

    In this case, the grace period for individuals whose residence visa has expired is usually 30 days. During this timeframe,you have to either renew your residence visa or make suitable arrangements to leave the country.

    It is crucial to understand that UAE immigration laws typically view exceeding the grace period as a breach. Overstaying can lead to penalties, fines, and potential bans on future entry to the country. It is better to comply with visa regulations and take appropriate measures within the grace period to prevent any legal complications.

    The renewal of a digital nomad visa is a smooth procedure. You must follow the same steps as the first time application process, and then wait for processing.

    The processing time for the renewal of the digital nomad visa can vary, but typically falls within the range of 30 to 60 days; this is why it is crucial to act as soon as the previous visa expires.

    Upon the approval of your renewal, you will be issued the renewed digital nomad visa, allowing you to continue living and working remotely in the UAE for another year.

    Your Digital Nomad Journey in Dubai

    Digital nomads are individuals who have the ability to travel without restrictions while performing their work remotely through the use of technology and the internet. They usually have few belongings and work from temporary lodgings like hotels, cafes, co-working spaces, or even mobile homes. They depend on Wi-Fi and mobile devices to maintain connectivity while on the move, thus the “nomad” in the name.

    A significant number of digital nomads are engaging in professions such as programming, content creation, design, and development. While some nomads prefer a constant journey across various countries, others opt to settle in a specific location; all while maintaining a flexible working space. The population of digital nomads has been consistently growing, with over 10.9 million individuals identifying as digital nomads in 2020, with a 49% increase in the upcoming year.

    Dubai is an appealing choice for digital nomads due to its modern infrastructure and lively way of life. The city presents a range of remote work possibilities, spanning sectors like hospitality, administration, engineering, and teaching. Moreover, the city boasts a variety of co-working spaces and cafes designed to cater to the specific needs of digital nomads, ensuring an ideal work setting.

    Additionally, Dubai’s free zones, which grant advantages in terms of import and customs duties, establish it as a key global hub for import and export activities. This creates abundant networking prospects, particularly for digital nomads engaged in frequent international business ventures.

    Conclusion

    In conclusion, the lifestyle of a digital nomad provides the liberty to discover diverse locations while simultaneously sustaining a means of earning. This is an ideal working opportunity for individuals employed by companies based outside of the UAE; as well as to business owners who have the ability to remotely manage their companies.

    Overall, the digital nomad visa in Dubai offers remote workers the chance to immerse themselves in the city’s dynamic lifestyle, advanced infrastructure, and promising business prospects, all while enjoying the advantages of working and living remotely.

    What is Withholding Tax?

    Withholding tax in Saudi Arabia, often referred to as Saudi Arabia withholding tax, is a key component of the country’s tax system. It functions as a mechanism where the source withholds a portion of income before it reaches the recipient, who can be an individual or a business entity.

    This tax serves two primary purposes. First, it ensures that the government collects taxes more efficiently by capturing a portion of the tax liability upfront. Second, it simplifies the tax collection process, especially for non-resident individuals and foreign businesses.

    In Saudi Arabia, withholding tax applies to various types of payments, such as those made to non-resident individuals or entities for services provided within the Kingdom. It also includes withholding tax on value-added tax (VAT) payments.

    For those wondering how to calculate withholding tax in Saudi Arabia, it is typically a straightforward process. The tax rate, which varies based on factors such as the recipient’s residency status, is applied to the payment amount. The withheld amount goes directly to the government through remittance.

    Understanding what withholding tax in Saudi Arabia is vital for individuals and businesses operating within the Kingdom. It ensures compliance with tax regulations, prevents potential penalties, and contributes to the smooth functioning of the country’s tax system.

Income tax withholding applies to payments made to non-resident individuals or entities for services within the Kingdom. In contrast, VAT withholding pertains to payments made by businesses to their suppliers.

    So, how do you calculate withholding tax in Saudi Arabia? The process is relatively straightforward. The payment amount has the applicable tax rate applied, which is determined by factors like the recipient’s residency status. The withheld amount is then remitted directly to the government.

    It is important to note that these regulations are not exclusive to Saudi Arabian residents. Non-resident individuals and foreign businesses must also adhere to withholding tax in KSA. Compliance ensures that everyone contributes to the country’s tax revenues, promoting fairness and equity.

    The significance of withholding tax in Saudi Arabia cannot be overstated. It streamlines tax compliance for non-residents, ensures a consistent influx of revenue for the government, and promotes responsible financial management for businesses.

    Types of Withholding Taxes in Saudi Arabia

How to start a business with a professional license in Dubai?

    Applying for a professional license in Dubai is a wise decision, as many people have lucrative businesses here. However, specific procedures and policies are needed to ensure everything is legal.

    The process for obtaining a professional license includes filling out all the paperwork and setting up an official company entity. This article will outline the steps to go ahead with this process and start your business.

    1. What is a professional license?

    A professional license in Dubai is a document that proves the person has met the required standards of the licensing authority to work in that profession.

    In the same way, to be eligible for this license, you must hold a bachelor’s degree and pass your professional exam. You will also need to complete several years of work experience before applying for the license.

    2. What are the most common types of professional licenses?

    2.1 Real estate agent license

    To become a real estate representative, you will need to obtain a real estate license. This type of license is among the most expensive. The Dubai Land Department (DLD) is responsible for issuing and regulating real estate licenses in Dubai.

    On the other hand, to opt for a real estate professional license in Dubai, you must have a valid UAE residency visa. This is the only way to start working as a real estate agent in Dubai.

    2.2 Engineering license

    An engineering license in Dubai is one of the most popular jobs for people interested in working in this field. However, the prices for this license are slightly more expensive.

    The engineering license is for people under the UAE Ministry of Higher Education and Scientific Research. The applicant should have completed their degree from an accredited university. They should also provide evidence that they have worked as a licensed engineer in their home country for not less than five years before applying.

    2.3 Medical license

    A medical license is necessary to work in Dubai. The medical license is for doctors under the Dubai Health Authority (DHA), and it is valid for five years. It can be renewed after five years if the doctor has not committed any violations or broken any rules.

    All doctors practicing in this country use a medical license to work in Dubai, regardless of nationality.

    2.4 Lawyer license

    The Dubai Legal Affairs Department (LAD) is the government authority responsible for the licensing and regulation of lawyers in Dubai. To be authorized as a lawyer in the city of Dubai, you must have a law degree from an accredited institution.

    Also, you need to pass the qualifying exams set by the LAD. Once you obtain your degree as a lawyer in Dubai, you can practice law in the UAE.

    2.5 Teacher license

    To work as a teacher in Dubai, you will need a professional license from the Dubai Teacher’s Licensing Department. The licensing process is straightforward, and most applicants get it without complications.

    To opt for a license in Dubai, you will need to have a degree in education from an accredited institution, and you must also have at least two years of teaching experience. You will also need to pass a check under your criminal background.

    2.6 Entertainment license

    You will need a sponsor from an established company in Dubai and a valid work permit to apply for the license. Also, you may also proof of your educational qualifications or any other certificates relevant to the type of work you are applying for.

    The company will need to ensure that you have all the necessary skills, qualifications, and experience listed in the job description.

    2.7 Financial advisors license

    Dubai is a great place to work as a financial advisor. Many expatriates in Dubai are looking for financial advice, and you can easily find clients through word-of-mouth or online advertising.

    To work as a financial advisor in Dubai, you must need the Dubai Financial Services Authority (DFSA) approval. The DFSA is the regulatory authority for the financial services industry in Dubai.

    2.8 Business consultant license

    Many business consultants would like to work in Dubai but may not have the necessary license. The good thing you need to know is that it is possible to get a business consultant license to work in Dubai.

    First, you need to determine if you meet the eligibility criteria for buying a consultant’s license. The requirements include meeting at least five years of experience or business management. You must also be proficient in Arabic because all business consultations are conducted in this language.

    2.9 Internet and web design license

    In the Emirates, there are few regulations for web designers. This means that anyone inside or outside the country can start designing websites as long as they have a UAE work visa. The cost for the internet license is affordable and easy to get

    3. The procedure to obtain a professional license to work in Dubai

    When applying for a professional license in the UAE, you should first provide a detailed overview of your company’s activities. The next move would be to hire a local service agent to handle all of the administrative tasks related to getting it.

    You need to get approval from the DED following your appointment. Apart from that, you should reserve a business name (for which you need to pay a fee) and then send all the paperwork to the DED for approval.

    3.1 Initial approval

    An initial approval means that the UAE Government has no objection to the business. However, this does not mean you have the right to operate your company. You will need to apply for permits and licenses before opening your business.

    Getting approval is necessary before or while undertaking some activities related to government resources. Examples of this are legal, security, and finances, which require approval before the initial approval.

    3.2 Register the trade name for your company

    You need to take a few steps to legally register your legal trade name in Dubai. The first step is to search the trade name registry to ensure the name you want is available. Once you have confirmed that another company is not using your company name, you can start the registration process.

    The trade name must not violate the country’s public morality or public order. The structure acronym must represent the legal form of the company. It is necessary to have a trading name compatible with the business entity and not registered before.

    3.3 Paperwork needed to apply for a professional license in Dubai

    The paperwork needed for applying for a professional license in Dubai is:

    • An application form
    • Passport copies of the expatriate business owners
    • ID copies of the expatriate business owners if they are residents
    • Visit visa copies if the expatriate business owners are not residents
    • Emirates ID copies and passport of the local partner
    • NOC (No Objection Certificate) from the expatriate business owner’s sponsor
    • Additional approvals listed by the Department of Economic Development
    • Licenses from the Municipality and Roads and Transport Authority (RTA) if necessary

    3.4 Get an application form

    Besides the documents already mentioned, to obtain your professional license in Dubai, you will need to present to the Dubai Municipality a prescribed application form (BR1 form). Also, you need the name reservation already certificated and the initial approval from the Department of Economic Development.

    You need to get the rental contract and the Ejari registration. The Ejari ensures the quality of the contracts, and it is necessary for professional license renewal in Dubai.

    3.5 Finish the application

    With the help of a local interpreter, fill out the Service Agreement Form. If the form is in Arabic, a legal translator seal is not required. Once you finish with that, create a contract with your sponsor by endowing them with a Memorandum of Association (MOA).

    Then, in the agreement, discuss the sponsor’s up-front fee. If you want to work for a civil company, you must fill out another registration form and get it certified. All business venture partners must appear to sign the court agreement if they want it to be considered valid.

    Finally, make sure you get permission from the place you will rent from the owner before signing the contract. A form submission requires an attestation (one original copy). Once you have it, send copies of your and the expatriate owner/partner’s passport cards to the branch.

    4. How much does a professional license cost?

    The costs of a professional license in Dubai will depend on the type of profession you wish to practice. Generally, the more specialized the job is, the more expensive is the license. These are of approximately AED 15,310 and include fees such as service agent fees, trade name fees, local fees, and many others.

    You have 30 days to make the payment for your registration from the date you receive the payment voucher statement. Otherwise, your application will not proceed, and you need to start the process again.

    5. Can a company have 100% ownership with a professional license?

    A DED professional license is one of the best aspects of opening a company in the emirates, and it gives you 100% ownership of your business. As long as you have a professional license, you only need an agreement with a local operator. Besides, the ownership of the equipment will be under your name.

    Having 100% foreign ownership is possible, but it depends on the business activity and the licensing category. A professional license in Dubai offers the most flexibility for foreign investors and carries out several positions under this license.

    6. How does the professional license renewal work?

    Renewing your license is a process you must do every year. For your comfort, the professional license activities in Dubai allow you to work for an entire year.

    You can do all the paperwork for the professional license renewal in Dubai from the DED after passing the license check. This includes an application form and a payment for the DED.

    7. How can a professional license help your company?

    The most evident benefit is that it can help you protect your company’s intellectual property. It can also help you set and enforce quality and professionalism standards within your industry.

    Passing the Dubai professional license check can also help build consumer trust by demonstrating that your company is committed to high quality and safety standards. In conclusion, professional licensing can also help attract new customers and business partners.
